metadata.title: Heat kernel for non-local operators with variable order

extraction_notes.note: Remark 1.5 has a sketched proof for its item (1) only; item (1) is emitted as a claim nested in the remark and the sketch proves that claim, while the remark's \ref to the sketch is kept as a mention.

Remark 2.2 states an integral estimate obtained from the proof of Chen-Zhang Lemma 2.1(i) and is used repeatedly; kept as an external remark rather than an external lemma because the environment is a remark and part of its text is commentary.
The Levi-method ansatz (p = p^y + correction, q solving an integral equation with kernel q_0) is typed as a definition of q_0, q and p rather than as an algorithm.

The lower bounds of Theorem 1.1 are proved in Corollary 5.10 via Propositions 5.6-5.9, whose proofs use the Chapman-Kolmogorov equation and generator identities (1.11), (1.15) that are proved in step (v) of the main proof; the argument is not circular, but at node granularity this gives a cycle through Theorem 1.1, kept as is.

The label t5-1-2 is used twice (Theorem 1.3 and Proposition 4.7); the parser resolves it to Theorem 1.3, so the \\eqref in the proof of Proposition 4.7 is kept only as a mention edge. References to the definition of rho (e3-0) and to equation (1.1) inside Theorem 1.1 are likewise marked as mentions.
The parser's structure for the proof of Proposition 2.9 misses the label Case (e) and the Subcases (c1)/(c2) in the proof of Lemma 3.1; steps were added for them by hand.
Corollary 5.10 has no proof environment; its justification is the lead-in sentence 'According to Propositions ... we immediately get the following', which has no closing punctuation.

Literature results mentioned in the Background (Bass, Chen-Kumagai, Chen-Zhang, Kolokoltsov) are only cited, not stated, and got no nodes; unnumbered displays and notational conventions inside proofs stay in their containing nodes.

metadata.extraction_comment: Most labelled proof steps follow the paper's (i)/(1)/Case labels only; long label bodies (some several pages) were not subdivided further.

nodes.name: Non-local operator of variable order L
differentia: $\kappa:\mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d \rightarrow (0,\infty)$ is a measurable function
nodes.statement_short: L f(x)=∫(f(x+z)-f(x)-⟨∇f(x),z⟩1_{|z|≤1}) κ(x,z)|z|^{-d-α(x)} dz with α Hölder, valued in [α_1,α_2]⊂(0,2), and κ symmetric in z, bounded between κ_1,κ_2 and Hölder in x.

nodes.statement: {\mathcal L} f(x)=\int_{\mathds R^d}\big(f(x+z)-f(x)-\langle\nabla f(x), z\rangle \mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}\big) \frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz,\quad f \in C_c^2(\mathds R^d),
nodes.name: Variable-order non-local operator L
nodes.label: e1-1

nodes.statement: \begin{split} & 0<\alpha_1\leqslant \alpha(x) \leqslant \alpha_2<2 \quad \hbox{for } x \in \mathds R^d,\\ & |\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|\leqslant c_1(|x-y|^{\beta_1}\wedge 1) \quad \hbox{for } x,y\in \mathds R^d, \end{split}
nodes.name: Conditions on the index function α
nodes.label: e1-3

nodes.statement: \begin{split} & \kappa(x,z)=\kappa(x,-z) \quad \hbox{for } x,z \in \mathds R^d,\\ & 0<\kappa_1\leqslant \kappa(x,z)\leqslant \kappa_2<\infty \quad \hbox{for } x,z\in \mathds R^d,\\ & |\kappa(x,z)-\kappa(y,z)|\leqslant c_2(|x-y|^{\beta_2}\wedge 1) \quad \hbox{for } x,y,z\in \mathds R^d, \end{split}
nodes.name: Conditions on the jump coefficient κ
nodes.label: e1-2

nodes.statement: Set $\beta_0= \beta_1\wedge \beta_2$.
nodes.name: Hölder exponent β_0

nodes.statement:
When
$\alpha(x)\equiv \alpha \in (0,2)$ and
$\kappa(x,z)\equiv \alpha2^{\alpha-1}\, \frac{\Gamma((\alpha+d)/2))}{\pi^{d/2}\,\Gamma(1-(\alpha/2))}$
for all $x,z\in\mathds R^d$,
${\mathcal L} $ of \eqref{e1-1} is the fractional Laplacian operator $-(-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}$, which is the infinitesimal generator of the rotationally symmetric $\alpha$-stable L\'evy process
in $\mathds R^d$.
Therefore ${\mathcal L}$ could be viewed as a generalization of fractional Laplacian operator with
jump coefficient $\kappa(x,z)$ and  of variable order  $\alpha(x)$.
nodes.name: Fractional Laplacian as a special case of L
nodes.statement_short: For constant α and a specific constant κ, L is the fractional Laplacian -(-Δ)^{α/2}, the generator of the rotationally symmetric α-stable process.

nodes.statement: For this reason, we call $\alpha(x)$ the order of the non-local operator at the point $x\in \mathds R^d$.
nodes.name: Order of the non-local operator
nodes.definiendum: order of the non-local operator at the point $x$

nodes.statement:
When $\alpha(x)$ is not a constant, how can we construct a fundamental solution of ${\mathcal L}$ that really satisfies
 the parabolic equation \eqref{t1-1-1} below?  What are upper
and lower bound estimates for this solution (if it exists)?
nodes.name: Construction and two-sided estimates of the fundamental solution of variable-order L
nodes.statement_short: For non-constant α(x), construct a fundamental solution of L satisfying the parabolic equation and find its upper and lower bounds.

nodes.statement:
When $\alpha(x)$ is not a constant and $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$, is there a strong Markov process
associated with ${\mathcal L}$?
nodes.name: Existence of a strong Markov process for variable-order L with z-dependent κ

nodes.statement: Can one establish regularity of the fundamental solution in some neighborhood of  $x_0$ (such  as  gradient estimate) in terms of $\alpha(x_0)$ under some special settings?
nodes.name: Regularity of the fundamental solution in terms of the local order α(x_0)

nodes.statement: For $x_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r>0$, define  $B(x_0, r):=\{x\in \mathds R^d: |x-x_0|<  r_0\}$.
nodes.name: Open ball B(x_0,r)

nodes.statement: Let $C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$ denote the set of all bounded and uniformly continuous functions on $\mathds R^d$.
nodes.name: Space C_{b,u} of bounded uniformly continuous functions
nodes.genus: the set of all bounded and uniformly continuous functions on $\mathds R^d$

nodes.statement: Suppose that conditions \eqref{e1-3} and \eqref{e1-2} hold. If $\kappa(x,z)= \kappa (x)$ is independent of $z$, then there exists a jointly continuous non-negative function $p:(0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d \rightarrow \mathds R_+:=[0,\infty)$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \frac{\partial p(t,x,y)}{\partial t}={\mathcal L} p(t,\cdot,y)(x), \end{equation} and has the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)]{\bf (Upper bounds)}\,\, For every $\gamma, c_0>0$, there exist positive constants $c_1 =c_1(\alpha,\kappa,c_0)$ and $c_2 =c_2(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,c_0)$ such that for all $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\leqslant \begin{cases} {c_1}{t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}},&\quad |x-y|< c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x)}},\\ \frac{c_1t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}\wedge \frac{c_2t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},&\quad c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |x-y|< 1,\\ \frac{c_1t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&\quad|x-y|\geqslant 1. \end{cases} \end{equation} If, in addition, there are some $x_0\in\mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for all $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$, then there is a positive constant $c_3 =c_3(\alpha,\kappa,r_0)$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\leqslant \begin{cases} \frac{c_3 t }{(t^{{1/\alpha(x_0)}}+|y-x_0|)^{d+\alpha(x_0)}},& |y-x_0|< {r_0}/{2},\\ \frac{c_3 t }{|y-x_0|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|y-x_0|\geqslant {r_0}/{2}; \end{cases} \end{equation} \noindent {\bf (Lower bounds)}\,\, There exists a constant $c_4 =c_4(\alpha,\kappa)>0$ such that for all $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\geqslant \frac{c_4t}{(t^{1/\alpha(x)}+|x-y|)^{d+\alpha(x)}}. \end{equation} \item[(ii)]{\bf (H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates)}\,\, For any $\gamma \in (0, \alpha_2]$, there exist positive constants $c_5 =c_5(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$ and $R_1=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x, x', y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x', y)\big| &\leqslant c_5 |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1} \big(\rho^{y,0}_{\gamma_0}(t,x-y)+\rho^{y,0}_{\gamma_0}(t,x'-y)\big), \end{split} \end{equation} where $\gamma_0= {\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}$ and \begin{equation} \rho_{\gamma}^{y,\beta}(t,x)=t^{\gamma}(|x|^{\beta}\wedge 1) \begin{cases} \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|x|)^{d+\alpha(y)}},& |x|\leqslant 1,\\ \frac{1}{|x|^{d+\alpha_1}},& |x|> 1. \end{cases} \end{equation} If moreover $\tilde \beta_0(x_0):=\big({\alpha_1\beta_0}/{\alpha(x_0)})\wedge \alpha_1>1-\alpha(x_0)$ for some $x_0 \in \mathds R^d$, then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x=x_0$. In this case, for every $\gamma>0$, $t\in(0,1]$ and $ y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\leqslant c_6 \, \rho^{y,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})+ (\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0^*/\alpha_1)-\gamma}(t,x_0-y) \end{equation} for some $c_6 =c_6(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,x_0)>0$, where $\beta_0^*:=\beta_0 \wedge\alpha_2$. \item[(iii)]{\bf (Chapman-Kolmogorov equation)} For every $s,t \in (0,1]$ with $s+t\leqslant 1$, \begin{equation} \int_{\mathds R^d}p(s,x,z)p(t,z,y)\,dz=p(s+t,x,y),\quad x,y\in \mathds R^d. \end{equation} \item[(iv)]{\bf (Conservativeness)} For every $(t,x)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)\,dy=1. \end{equation} \item[(v)] {\bf (Strong continuity and generator)} For every $f \in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$, let $$u_f(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy.$$ Then \begin{equation} {\mathcal L} u_f (t, \cdot) (x) \hbox{ exists pointwise}, \quad t \mapsto {\mathcal L} u_f (t, ) (x) \hbox{ is continuous}, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \frac{\partial u_f(t,x)}{\partial t} = {\mathcal L} u_f(t,\cdot)(x), \quad t\in (0,1],\ x \in \mathds R^d, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}|u_f(t,x)-f(x)|=0. \end{equation} For every $f \in C_{b,u}^2(\mathds R^d):= C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)\cap C^2(\mathds R^d)$, we also have \begin{equation} \frac{\partial u_f(t,x)}{\partial t}=\int_{\mathds R^d} p(t,x,y){\mathcal L} f(y)\,dy,\quad t\in (0,1],\ x \in \mathds R^d \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}\Big|\frac{1}{t}\cdot\big( u_f(t,x)-f(x)\big)-{\mathcal L} f(x)\Big|=0. \end{equation} \item[(vi)] {\bf (Uniqueness)} Jointly continuous function $p(t, x, y)$ on $(0, 1]\times \mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d$ that is bounded for each $t>0$ and satisfies \eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-2a}-\eqref{t1-1-3} is unique. \end{enumerate}

nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item [(1)] From \eqref{t1-1-4} and \eqref{t1-1-4b}, we know that both upper and lower bounds of near-diagonal estimates for $p(t,x,y)$ enjoy the same order $t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}$, which typically depends on $x$. In particular, along with \eqref{t1-1-4b}, when $r_0=\infty$ in \eqref{t1-1-4a} (i.e.\ $\alpha(x)\equiv \alpha \in (0,2)$ for all $x\in \mathds R^d$), we arrive at the two-sided heat kernel estimates obtained in \cite{CZ}. Furthermore, by \eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-7a}, the regularity of $p(t,\cdot,y)$ at $x=x_0$ only depends on $x_0$. \item [(2)] Compared with these results yielded by Duhamel's formula in \cite{Kol}, Theorem \ref{t1-1}(v) shows that the function $u_f(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy$ solves the Cauchy problem for ${\mathcal L}$. In particular, by \eqref{t1-1-1} and \eqref{t1-1-3}, we have \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} \frac{\partial }{\partial t} p(t,x,y) = {\mathcal L} p(t,\cdot,y)(x)\\ \lim_{t \downarrow 0} p(t,x,y)=\delta_y(x), \end{cases} \end{equation*} which means that $p(t,x,y)$ is the fundamental solution associated with ${\mathcal L}$. It is easy to deduce from \eqref{t1-1-7}, \eqref{t1-1-5}, \eqref{t1-1-6}, \eqref{t1-1-2} and \eqref{t1-1-5a} that there is a conservative Feller process having the strong Feller property associated with the operator ${\mathcal L}$; cf. Proposition \ref{p4-4} below. Recall that a Markov process on $\mathds R^d$ is said to be a Feller process if its transition semigroup is a strongly continuous semigroup in the Banach space of continuous functions that vanish at infinity equipped with the uniform norm. A Markov process is said to have the strong Feller property if its transition semigroup maps bounded measurable functions to bounded continuous functions. \end{itemize}
nodes.name: Remark 1.2 (consequences of Theorem 1.1)
nodes.statement_short: Near-diagonal bounds have order t^{-d/α(x)}; constant α recovers Chen-Zhang; p is the fundamental solution and yields a conservative strong Feller process.

nodes.statement: Let $\beta_0^{**}\in(0,\beta_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ For general $\kappa (x, z)$ satisfying \eqref{e1-3} and \eqref{e1-2}, if $ ({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<\beta_0^{**}/{\alpha_2}, $ there exists a jointly continuous non-negative function $p:(0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d \rightarrow \mathds R_+$ such that all the conclusions in Theorem $\ref{t1-1}$ hold except that the upper bounds \eqref{t1-1-4}-\eqref{t1-1-4a} in {\rm (i)} and H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates \eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-7a} in {\rm (ii)} are to be replaced by the following estimates. \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)]{\bf (Upper bounds)}\,\, For any $\gamma, c_0>0$, there exist constants $c_1 =c_1(\alpha,\kappa,c_0)>0$ and $c_2 =c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,c_0)>0$ such that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\leqslant \begin{cases} {c_1}{t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}},&\quad |x-y|< c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}, \smallskip \\ \frac{c_1t^{2-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}} \wedge \frac{c_2t^{2-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},&\quad c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |x-y|< 1, \smallskip \\ \frac{c_1t^{2-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&\quad |x-y|\geqslant 1. \end{cases} \end{equation} If, in addition, there are some $x_0\in\mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for all $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$, then for any $c_0>0$ there is a positive constant $c_3:=c_3(\alpha,\kappa,r_0,c_0)$ so that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\leqslant \begin{cases} {c_3}{t^{-{d/\alpha (x_0)}}},&\quad |y-x_0|< c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x_0)}}, \smallskip \\ \frac{c_3 t^{2-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})} }{|y-x_0|^{d+\alpha(x_0)}},& \quad c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x_0)}}\leqslant |y-x_0|< {r_0}/{2}, \smallskip \\ \frac{c_3 t^{2-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})} }{|x-y_0|^{d+\alpha_1}},&\quad |y-x_0|\geqslant {r_0}/{2}. \end{cases} \end{equation} \item[(ii)] {\bf (H\"{o}lder regularity and gradient estimates)}\,\, For every $\gamma \in (0, \alpha_1]$, there exist constants $c_5 =c_5(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$ and $R_1 =R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,x',y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big| &\leqslant c_5|x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1} \big(\rho^{y,0}_{\gamma_1}(t,x-y)+ \rho^{y,0}_{\gamma_1}(t,x'-y)\big), \end{split} \end{equation} where $\gamma_1:=1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))$. Let $\beta_0^*$ and $\tilde \beta_0(x_0)$ be the same constants in Theorem $\ref{t1-1}$ $(ii)$. If moreover $\tilde \beta_0(x_0)-({\alpha_1\alpha_2}/{\alpha(x_0)}) \big(({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1\big)>1-\alpha_1$ for some $x_0\in \mathds R^d$, then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x=x_0$. In this case, for every $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant $c_6:=c_6(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma, x_0)$ such that for all $ t\in (0,1]$ and $y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\leqslant c_6 \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha_1)+(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0^*/\alpha_1)-\gamma_2}(t,x_0-y), \end{equation} where $\gamma_2=(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)-1+\gamma.$ \end{enumerate}

nodes.statement_short: For general κ(x,z), if (α_2/α_1)-1 < β_0^{**}/α_2 (small oscillation of α), L has a heat kernel with all conclusions of Theorem 1.1 except for weaker upper bounds and regularity estimates.

nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item[(1)] According to Theorem \ref{t1-2} above, when $\alpha(x)$ is not a constant function and $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$, we can construct heat kernel associated with the operator ${\mathcal L}$ when $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<\beta_0^{**}/{\alpha_2}$, which indicates that the oscillation of the index function $\alpha(x)$ could not be too large. We note that in \cite{BK2}, the elliptic Harnack inequality for ${\mathcal L}$ was established under similar assumptions on the index function $\alpha(x)$. Note that by \eqref{t1-1-9a} and \eqref{t1-1-4b}, when $\alpha(x)\equiv \alpha \in (0,2)$ for all $x\in \mathds R^d$, two-sided estimates of heat kernel in Theorem \ref{t1-2} are reduced to those in \cite{CZ}. \item[(2)] As mentioned in Remark \ref{remark1}(2), Theorem \ref{t1-2} indeed provides us some sufficient conditions for the existence of a strong Markov process (in fact a Feller process having the strong Feller property) associated with ${\mathcal L}$ when $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$. Note that, the existence of such strong Markov process is required and assumed a prior in the proofs of the H\"{o}lder continuity of harmonic functions in \cite{BK1} and the elliptic Harnack inequality for ${\mathcal L}$ in \cite{BK2}. \end{enumerate}
nodes.name: Remark 1.4 (on Theorem 1.3)
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1.3 needs small oscillation of α, reduces to Chen-Zhang for constant α, and gives a strong Markov process for z-dependent κ.

nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] By carefully checking the arguments of Theorem \ref{t1-1}, one can see that Theorem \ref{t1-1} still holds true if the condition that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$ is replaced by the following two assumptions on $\kappa(x,z)$: \begin{itemize} \item [(i)] For every fixed $x \in \mathds R^d$, $\kappa(x,\cdot):\mathds R^d \rightarrow \mathds R_+$ is a radial function, i.e., $\kappa(x,z)$ only depends on $|z|$. \item [(ii)] Let $j(x,r)=\widetilde \kappa(x,r)r^{-d-\alpha(x)}$ for $x \in \mathds R^d$ and $r>0$, where $\widetilde \kappa(x,r):=\kappa(x,z)$ with $|z|=r$. For every $x \in \mathds R^d$, $j(x,\cdot)$ is non-increasing and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ such that the function $r\mapsto -\frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial j(x,r)}{\partial r}$ is non-increasing. \end{itemize} \item[(2)] Let $\widetilde {\mathcal L} f(x)={\mathcal L} f(x)+\langle b(x), \nabla f(x)\rangle$, where $b:\mathds R^d\rightarrow \mathds R^d$ is bounded and uniformly H\"older continuous. It is possible to extend Theorems \ref{t1-1} and \ref{t1-2} to $\widetilde {\mathcal L}$ under the assumption that $\alpha_1>1$, When $\alpha_1>1$, the gradient perturbation $\langle b(x), \nabla \rangle$ is of lower order than ${\mathcal L}$. We refer the readers to \cite{BJ, CD, CH, JS, MM, MM1,XZ} on heat kernel estimates associated with non-local operators under gradient perturbation. For heat kernel estimates associated with non-local operators under non-local perturbations, see \cite{CW, W, CHXZ}. \item[(3)] By combining with the approach from \cite{CZ4}, it is possible to remove the symmetry assumption of $\kappa (x, z)$ in $z$. But we will not pursue this extension in this paper. \end{itemize}
nodes.name: Remark 1.5 (possible extensions)
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1.1 extends to radial κ with monotone jump profile; gradient perturbations and non-symmetric κ may also be treated.

\item [(i)] For every fixed $x \in \mathds R^d$, $\kappa(x,\cdot):\mathds R^d \rightarrow \mathds R_+$

nodes.statement:
According to the Levi's method (cf. \cite[pp.\ 310--311]{Fi}), we
look for the fundamental solution to \eqref{t1-1-1} of the following
form:
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
& p(t,x,y)=p^y(t,x-y)+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds,
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where $q(t,x,y)$ solves
\begin{equation} q(t,x,y)=q_0(t,x,y)+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}q_0(t-s,x,z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds
\end{equation}
with
$
q_0(t,x,y)=( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y)p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y).
$

nodes.statement:
For each fixed $y \in \mathds R^d$, $\beta \in [0,\infty)$, $\gamma\in \mathds R$ and $R \in (0,\infty)$, we
define a function
$\rho_{\gamma,R}^{y,\beta}:(0,1]\times \mathds R^d \rightarrow (0,\infty)$ as follows
\begin{equation*}
\rho_{\gamma,R}^{y,\beta}(t,x):=t^{\gamma}\big(|x|^{\beta}\wedge 1\big)
\begin{cases}
 \big(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|x|\big)^{-(d+\alpha(y))},&  |x|\leqslant R,\\
 |x|^{-(d+\alpha_1)},& |x|> R,
\end{cases}
\end{equation*} where $\alpha(x)$ is the index function in \eqref{e1-1} and $\alpha_1$
is the lower bound of $\alpha (x)$  in \eqref{e1-3}.

c\rho_{\gamma,R_1}^{y,\beta}$ for all $y\in \mathds R^d$ and $\beta\in[0,\infty)$.

nodes.statement: Since $\beta\in (0,\alpha_2)$, it suffices to prove the first inequality in \eqref{l3-1-1}. For every $x,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-z|\leqslant 1$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} |x-z|^{-\alpha(z)}&=|x-z|^{-\alpha(x)}|x-z|^{\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)}\preceq |x-z|^{-\alpha(x)}\cdot \exp\left(\left|\log|x-z|\right|\left|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)\right|\right)\\ &\preceq |x-z|^{-\alpha(x)}\cdot \exp\left(C\left|\log|x-z|\right|\cdot |x-z|^{\beta_0}\right) \preceq |x-z|^{-\alpha(x)}, \end{split} \end{equation} where in the last inequality we have used $$\sup_{z\in \mathds R^d: |z|\leqslant 1}\exp\big(C|\log |z||\cdot|z|^{\beta_0}\big)<\infty.$$ Then, for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,z\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{align*} \frac{1}{(t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}+|x-z|)^{d+\alpha(z)}}& \preceq \begin{cases} |x-z|^{-d-\alpha(z)},& |x-z|\leqslant 1,\\ t^{-1-({d/\underline{\alpha}(x; t^{1/\alpha_2})})},& |x-z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}, \end{cases} \\ &\preceq \begin{cases} |x-z|^{-d-\alpha(x)},& |x-z|\leqslant 1,\\ t^{-1-({d/\underline{\alpha}(x; t^{1/\alpha_2})})},& |x-z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}. \end{cases} \end{align*} Therefore, by the definition of $\rho_{0}^{z,\beta}$ (see \eqref{e3-0}), for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$, we have \begin{align*} \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho_{0}^{z,\beta}(t,x-z)\,dz \preceq& \int_{\{|z-x|> 1\}}\frac{1}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dz + \int_{\{t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}<|z-x|\leqslant 1\}}\frac{|x-z|^{\beta}}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &+t^{-1-({d/\underline{\alpha}(x; t^{1/\alpha_2})})}\int_{\{|z-x|\leqslant t^{1/\alpha(x)}\}} |x-z|^{\beta}\,dz\\ =&:J_1+J_2+J_3. \end{align*} It is easy to verify that $J_1\preceq 1$ and $J_2\preceq \big(t^{(\beta-\alpha(x))/{\alpha(x)}}\vee 1\big) \big(1+|\log t|\mathds 1_{\{\beta=\alpha(x)\}}\big)$, due to the assumption that $\beta\in [0,\alpha_2)$. At the same time, \begin{align*} J_3&\preceq t^{-1-({d/\underline{\alpha}(x; t^{1/\alpha_2}}))}\cdot t^{(\beta+d)/\alpha(x)} \preceq t^{(\beta-\alpha(x))/\alpha(x)}\exp\left(d|\log t| \frac{\alpha(x)-\underline{\alpha}(x;t^{{1/\alpha_2}}) }{\alpha(x)\underline{\alpha}(x;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}\right) \\ &\preceq t^{(\beta-\alpha(x))/\alpha(x)}\exp\big(c|\log t| t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}\big)\preceq t^{{(\beta-\alpha(x))}/{\alpha(x)}}, \end{align*} where in the forth inequality we have used $$ \frac{\alpha(x)-\underline{\alpha}(x;t^{{1/\alpha_2}}) }{\alpha(x)\underline{\alpha}(x;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}\preceq t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}, $$ thanks to \eqref{e1-3}. Combining all the estimates above, we get the first inequality in \eqref{l3-1-1}. The proof is complete.

Therefore, by the definition of $\rho_{0}^{z,\beta}$ (see \eqref{e3-0}), for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$, we have
\begin{align*}
\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho_{0}^{z,\beta}(t,x-z)\,dz \preceq&
\int_{\{|z-x|> 1\}}\frac{1}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dz +
\int_{\{t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}<|z-x|\leqslant 1\}}\frac{|x-z|^{\beta}}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&+t^{-1-({d/\underline{\alpha}(x; t^{1/\alpha_2})})}\int_{\{|z-x|\leqslant t^{1/\alpha(x)}\}}
|x-z|^{\beta}\,dz\\
=&:J_1+J_2+J_3.
\end{align*}


It is easy to verify that $J_1\preceq 1$  and $J_2\preceq \big(t^{(\beta-\alpha(x))/{\alpha(x)}}\vee 1\big)
\big(1+|\log t|\mathds 1_{\{\beta=\alpha(x)\}}\big)$, due to the assumption that $\beta\in [0,\alpha_2)$.

At the same time,
\begin{align*}

&\preceq t^{(\beta-\alpha(x))/\alpha(x)}\exp\big(c|\log t| t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}\big)\preceq t^{{(\beta-\alpha(x))}/{\alpha(x)}},
\end{align*}
where in the forth inequality we have used
$$
\frac{\alpha(x)-\underline{\alpha}(x;t^{{1/\alpha_2}}) }{\alpha(x)\underline{\alpha}(x;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}\preceq t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}},

nodes.statement: By the proof of \cite[Lemma 2.1(i)]{CZ}, we can obtain that for every $\beta \in [0,\alpha_2)$, $t \in (0,1]$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho_{0}^{x,\beta}(t,x-z)\,dz\preceq \big(t^{({\beta}/{\alpha(x)})-1}\vee 1\big)\big(1+|\log t|\mathds 1_{\{\beta=\alpha(x)\}}\big)\preceq t^{({\beta}/{\alpha_2})-1}\vee 1. \end{equation} Note that although the definition of $\rho^{x,\beta}_{0}(t,x)$ here is a little different from that in \cite{CZ} when $|x|>1$, the proof of \cite[Lemma 2.1]{CZ} still works for the first inequality in \eqref{l3-1-1-00}. We emphasize that in the present setting we need estimate \eqref{l3-1-1}, where in the integrand $\rho^{z,\beta}_0$ the index $\alpha(z)$ depends on $z$.

nodes.statement: For every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,w\in \mathds R^d$, define \begin{equation} \begin{split} I_1(t,x,y,w):=&\int_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \rho^{y,0}_1(t,w + z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz,\\ I_2(t,x,y,w):=&\int_{\{|z|>1\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w + z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz,\\ I_3(t,x,y):=&\int_{\mathds R^d}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \left( \frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}} +\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\right)\,dz. \end{split} \end{equation} Then there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa)$ such that for every $x,y,w \in \mathds R^d$ and $t \in (0,1]$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} I_1(t,x,y,w) \leqslant \begin{cases} c_1(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ & |w|\leqslant {1}/{2},\\ c_1\big[1+|\log|w||+(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\big]\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ & |w|> {1}/{2}; \end{cases}\end{split} \end{equation} \begin{equation} I_2(t,x,y,w)\leqslant \begin{cases} c_1\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w),\ & |w|\leqslant {1}/{2},\\ c_1\big(1+|\log|w||\big)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ & |w|>{1}/{2}; \end{cases} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} I_3(t,x,y)\leqslant c_1(1+|\log t|)t^{-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Lemma 2.3 (estimates of I_1, I_2, I_3)
nodes.statement_short: Bounds for three auxiliary integrals of ρ against variable-index jump kernels, in terms of ρ_0^{y,0}(t,w) and log factors.

nodes.statement: We only prove \eqref{l1-1-1} and \eqref{l1-1-2}, since the proof of \eqref{l1-1-3} is similar and more direct. We denote $I_1(t,x,y,w)$ and $I_2(t,x,y,w)$ by $I_1$ and $I_2$, respectively. Write \begin{align*} I_1&=\int_{\{|z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}} \big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz +\int_{\{t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}<|z|\leqslant 1\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\ &=:I_{11}+I_{12}. \end{align*} We will divide the proof into the following three subcases. {\bf Case (a): $0\leqslant |w| \leqslant 2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$.} Since, by \eqref{e3-0}, \begin{equation} \rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(y)}}\quad \textrm{ for all } t\in(0,1]\textrm{ and } y,z,w\in\mathds R^d,\end{equation} we have \begin{align*} I_{11}&\preceq t^{-{(d+2)}/{\alpha(y)}}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}} \frac{(1+|\log|z|)|z|^2}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\ &\preceq(1+|\log t|)t^{-{(d+\overline\alpha(y;x))}/{\alpha(y)}} \preceq(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w), \end{align*} where in the last inequality we have used the fact that \begin{equation}t^{-{d/\alpha(y)}}\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1(t,w) \quad \textrm{ when } |w|\leqslant 2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}.\end{equation} Applying \eqref{e:ond} and \eqref{e:one1} to $I_{12}$ and $I_2$ again, we get \begin{align*} I_{12}&\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(y)}}\int_{\{t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}<|z|\leqslant 1\}} \frac{1+|\log |z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz \preceq(1+|\log t|)t^{-({d+\overline\alpha(y;x)})/{\alpha(y)}}\\ & \preceq(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline \alpha(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w) \end{align*} and \begin{align*} I_2&\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(y)}}\int_{\{|z|> 1\}} \frac{1+\log |z|}{|z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dz\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1(t,w). \end{align*} {\bf Case (b): $2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}<|w|\leqslant {1}/{2}$.} When $|w|>2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ and $|z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, $ |w{+} z|\geqslant |w|-{|w|}/{2}\geqslant {|w|}/{2}, $ which along with \eqref{e3-0} implies that \begin{equation} \begin{split} \rho^{y,0}_0(t,w{+} z)&\preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|w{+} z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}\preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|w|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}. \end{split} \end{equation} Therefore, \begin{align*} I_{11}&\preceq \frac{t^{1-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|w|)^{d+\alpha(y)}} \int_{\{|z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}\frac{(1+|\log |z||)|z|^2}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\ & \preceq (1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline\alpha(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|w|)^{d+\alpha(y)}} \preceq (1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline \alpha(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w), \end{align*} where the last step is due to the fact that \begin{equation}\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|w|)^{d+\alpha(y)}} \preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,w)\quad \textrm{ when }|w|>2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}.\end{equation} On the other hand, we have the following decomposition for $I_{12}$: \begin{align*} I_{12}&=\int_{\{ t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}<|z|\leqslant{|w|}/{2}\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z) \frac{1+|\log |z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz + \int_{\{{|w|}/{2}\leqslant |z|\leqslant 1\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z) \frac{1+|\log |z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\ &=:I_{121}+I_{122}. \end{align*} If $|z|\leqslant {|w|}/{2}$, then $|w{+} z|\geqslant {|w|}/{2}$, and so \eqref{l2-1-7} still holds. Hence, we have \begin{align*} I_{121}&\preceq \frac{t}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|w|)^{d+\alpha(y)}} \int_{\{|z|>t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}\frac{1+|\log |z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\ &\preceq (1+|\log t|)t^{-{\overline \alpha(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)}}\frac{t}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|w|)^{d+\alpha(y)}} \preceq (1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline \alpha(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w), \end{align*} where the last step follows from \eqref{e:one-2}. Meanwhile, \begin{align*} I_{122}&\preceq \frac{1+|\log|w||}{|w|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\,dz\preceq \frac{1+|\log|w||}{|w|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\\ &\preceq \frac{(1+|\log|w||)|w|^{\alpha(y)-\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|w|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}\preceq (1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w), \end{align*} where the second inequality is due to \eqref{l3-1-1-00}, in the third inequality we have used the fact that $$|w|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq (t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|w|)^{-d-\alpha(y)}\quad \textrm{ when } 2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}<|w|\leqslant {1}/{2},$$ and the fourth inequality follows from $$ (1+|\log|w||)|w|^{\alpha(y)-\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}\preceq (1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})} \quad\textrm{ when }2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}<|w|\leqslant {1}/{2}.$$ Combining with all the estimates above, we obtain $$I_1\preceq (1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w).$$ Furthermore, note that if $|w|\leqslant {1}/{2}$ and $|z|>1$, then $ |w{+} z|\geqslant |z|-|w|\geqslant 2|w|-|w|=|w|. $ Therefore, for every $y,z,w\in\mathds R^d$ and $t\in(0,1]$ with $|z|>1$ and $2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\leqslant |w|\leqslant{1}/{2}$, \begin{align*} \rho^{y,0}_0(t,w{+} z)& \preceq \begin{cases} |w|^{-d-\alpha(y)}, \ &\ |w{+} z|\leqslant 1,\\ |w|^{-d-\alpha_1},\ &\ |w{+} z|> 1 \end{cases}\\ &\preceq |w|^{-d-\alpha(y)}, \end{align*} which implies that \begin{align*} I_2&\preceq \frac{t}{|w|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \int_{\{|z|\geqslant 1\}} \frac{1+\log |z|}{|z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dz\preceq \frac{t}{|w|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1(t,w). \end{align*} {\bf{Case (c): $|w|>{1}/{2}$}.} By adjusting the constants properly, it is easy to verify that \begin{align*} I_1+I_2&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {1}/{4}\}}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz +\int_{\{|z|>{1}/{4}\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\ &=:J_1+J_2. \end{align*} Note that when $|w|>{1}/{2}$ and $|z|\leqslant {1}/{4}$, $|w{+} z|\geqslant |w|-|z|\geqslant {|w|}/{2}>{1}/{4}$, which implies that $$\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\preceq \frac{t}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}}.$$ On the other hand, \begin{align*} &\int_{{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\ &\preceq \int_{{\{|z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}}\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big) \frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz+\int_{\{t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}<|z|\leqslant 1\}}\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\ &\preceq (1+|\log t|)t^{-{\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)}}. \end{align*} Therefore, we obtain \begin{align*} J_1&\preceq \frac{t}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}} \int_{{\{|z|\leqslant {1}/{4}\}}}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\ &\preceq \frac{\big(1+|\log t|\big)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \big(1+|\log t|\big)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w). \end{align*} Meanwhile, \begin{align*} J_2&\preceq \int_{\{|z|>{|w|}/{2}\}}\!\!\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz +\! \int_{\{{1}/{4}<|z|<{|w|}/{2}\}}\!\!\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\ &\preceq \frac{1+|\log|w||}{|w|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}} \int_{\{|z|>{|w|}/{2}\}}\!\! \rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\,dz +\! \frac{t}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}}\int_{\{|z|>{1}/{4}\}}\!\!\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dz\\ &\preceq \frac{1+|\log |w||}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq (1+|\log |w||)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w), \end{align*} where the second step above follows from the following property \begin{equation*} \rho^{y,0}_0(t,w{+} z)\preceq |w|^{-d-\alpha_1}\quad \textrm{ when } |z|<{|w|}/{2}\textrm{ and }\ |w|>{1}/{2}, \end{equation*} and the third step is due to \eqref{l3-1-1-00}. Hence, for all $w\in \mathds R^d$ with $|w|>{1}/{2}$, $$ I_1\preceq J_1+J_2\preceq \big[1+|\log |w||+(1+|\log t|)t^{-{\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)}}\big]\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w)$$ and $$ I_2\preceq J_2\preceq (1+|\log |w||)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w). $$ Combining all the three cases together, we finish the proof.

{\bf{Case (c): $|w|>{1}/{2}$}.}

By adjusting the constants properly, it is easy to verify that
\begin{align*}
I_1+I_2&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {1}/{4}\}}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big]
\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz +\int_{\{|z|>{1}/{4}\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{align*}
Note that when $|w|>{1}/{2}$ and $|z|\leqslant {1}/{4}$,
$|w{+} z|\geqslant |w|-|z|\geqslant {|w|}/{2}>{1}/{4}$, which implies
that
$$\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\preceq \frac{t}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}}.$$ On the other hand,
\begin{align*}
&\int_{{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big]
\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \int_{{\{|z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}}\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)
\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz+\int_{\{t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}<|z|\leqslant 1\}}\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq (1+|\log t|)t^{-{\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)}}.
\end{align*}
Therefore, we obtain
\begin{align*}
J_1&\preceq \frac{t}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}} \int_{{\{|z|\leqslant {1}/{4}\}}}\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big]
\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{\big(1+|\log t|\big)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \big(1+|\log t|\big)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w).
\end{align*}
Meanwhile,
\begin{align*}
J_2&\preceq \int_{\{|z|>{|w|}/{2}\}}\!\!\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz +\!
\int_{\{{1}/{4}<|z|<{|w|}/{2}\}}\!\!\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq
\frac{1+|\log|w||}{|w|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}} \int_{\{|z|>{|w|}/{2}\}}\!\!
\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w{+} z)\,dz +\!
\frac{t}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}}\int_{\{|z|>{1}/{4}\}}\!\!\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{1+|\log |w||}{|w|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq (1+|\log |w||)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),
\end{align*}
where the second step above follows from  the following property
\begin{equation*}
\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w{+} z)\preceq |w|^{-d-\alpha_1}\quad \textrm{ when }
|z|<{|w|}/{2}\textrm{ and }\ |w|>{1}/{2},
\end{equation*}
and the third step is due to \eqref{l3-1-1-00}.
Hence, for all $w\in \mathds R^d$ with $|w|>{1}/{2}$,
$$ I_1\preceq J_1+J_2\preceq \big[1+|\log |w||+(1+|\log t|)t^{-{\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)}}\big]\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w)$$ and
$$ I_2\preceq J_2\preceq  (1+|\log |w||)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w).
$$
Combining all the three cases together,  we finish the proof.

Then there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa, \gamma, r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in(0,1]$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y_0)|\leqslant c_1\big(|x-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \begin{cases} \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y_0)}}+|x-y_0|)^{d+\alpha(y_0)}},& |x-y_0|< r_0,\\ \frac{1}{|x-y_0|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|x-y_0|\geqslant r_0. \end{cases} \end{equation} \item[(2)] For general $\kappa (x, z)$ and for any $\gamma>0$, there are constants $R_0:=R_0(\alpha,\kappa, \gamma)\in(0,1)$ and $c_0:=c_0(\alpha,\kappa, \gamma)>0$ such that for all $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} |q_0(t,x,y)|\leqslant& c_0\big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \begin{cases} \frac{t^{-\gamma}}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|x-y|)^{d+\alpha(y)}},& |x-y|< R_0,\\ \frac{t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}, &|x-y|\geqslant R_0 \end{cases}\\ \preceq&\rho_{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y).\end{split} \end{equation} Suppose, in addition, that there are some $y_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y_0)|\leqslant c_1\big(|x-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \begin{cases} \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y_0)}}+|x-y_0|)^{d+\alpha(y_0)}},& |x-y_0|< r_0,\\ \frac{t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}}{|x-y_0|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|x-y_0|\geqslant r_0. \end{cases} \end{equation} \end{itemize}

nodes.statement: $($\cite[Lemmas 2.2 and 2.3]{CZ}$)$ The following statements hold. \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\kappa(x,z) =\kappa (x)$ is independent of $z$, then for any $j \in \mathbb{Z}_+:=\{0,1,\ldots\}$, there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa, j)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} |\nabla^j p^y(t,\cdot)(x)|\leqslant c_1t\big(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|x|\big)^{-d-\alpha(y)-j}. \end{equation} \item[(2)] For general $\kappa(x,z)$, there exists a constant $c_2:=c_2(\alpha,\kappa)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,x',y,z \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} p^y(t,x)\leqslant c_2 \rho_1^{y,0}(t,x), \end{equation} \begin{equation} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)|\leqslant c_2\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot \big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x)\big), \end{equation} \begin{equation} \begin{split} |p^y(t,x)-p^y(t,x')|&\leqslant c_2\big[\big(t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|x-x'|\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot\big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x')+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x)\big), \end{split} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \begin{split} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x';z)|& \leqslant c_2 \big[\big(t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|x-x'|\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot \big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big]\\ &\quad\times\big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x')\big). \end{split} \end{equation} \end{itemize}

nodes.statement: (i) Applying the mean value theorem to the function $r\mapsto a^r$, we find that for every $x,y,z \in \mathds R^d$ with $|z|>0$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg|\\ &\preceq |\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|\bigg(\frac{|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+ \frac{\log|z|}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg) +\frac{|\kappa(x,z)-\kappa(y,z)|}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\ &\preceq \big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\bigg(\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline \alpha(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+ \frac{1+\log|z|}{|z|^{d+\underline \alpha(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg), \end{split} \end{equation} where in the last inequality we have used \eqref{e1-2}, \eqref{e1-3} and the fact that \begin{equation*} \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\preceq \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\overline \alpha(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+ \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\underline \alpha(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}. \end{equation*} Combining \eqref{e:pp} with \eqref{e2-3}, we can obtain that \begin{align*} \big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t,w)\big| & \preceq \big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big) \int_{\mathds R^d}|\delta_{p^y}(t,w;z)|\bigg( \frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg)\,dz\\ &\preceq\big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \big(I_1(t,x,y,w)+I_2(t,x,y,w)+\rho^{y,0}_1(t,w)I_3(t,x,y)\big), \end{align*} where in the second inequality we have used \eqref{p1-1-2}, and $I_1$, $I_2$ and $I_3$ are defined in \eqref{l1-1-0}. Hence, Lemma \ref{l1-1} yields that \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t,w)\big|\\ &\preceq \!\big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big) \!\cdot\! \begin{cases} (1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ \ &\ |w|\leqslant {1}/{2},\\ \big(1+|\log |w||+(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\big)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ \ &\ |w|>{1}/{2}. \end{cases} \end{split} \end{equation} Note that due to \eqref{e1-3}, \begin{equation*} \overline{\alpha}(y;x)\leqslant \alpha(y)+c_0|x-y|^{\beta_0}\leqslant \alpha(y)+c_0R_1^{\beta_0}\quad\textrm{ for all } x,y\in\mathds R^d\textrm{ with }|x-y|\leqslant R_1. \end{equation*} Therefore, choosing $R_1\in(0,{1}/{2})$ small enough such that $c_0R_1^{\beta_0} /\alpha_1 < \gamma$, we have \begin{equation*} (1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\preceq t^{-\gamma}\quad\textrm{ when }|x-y|\leqslant R_1. \end{equation*} This, along with \eqref{l1-2-2}, immediately implies \eqref{l1-2-1}. Estimate \eqref{l1-2-1a} follows from \eqref{l1-2-1} by taking $w=x-y$. \smallskip (ii) Suppose, in addition, that there are some $y_0\in\mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(x)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $x \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then \eqref{e:pp} is reduced to \begin{equation*} \begin{split} &\bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y_0,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y_0)}}\bigg|\preceq \big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot\bigg(\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y_0)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+ \frac{1}{|z|^{d+ \alpha(y_0)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg) \end{split} \end{equation*} for all $x\in B(y_0,r_0)$. Having this at hand and repeating the same argument above, we can easily see that the second assertion holds in this case.
nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.7 (estimate of (L^x-L^y)p^y)
nodes.statement_short: Mean value estimate of the kernel difference in α and κ, combined with the second-difference bound for p^y and Lemma 2.3; R_1 chosen small to absorb the log factor.

nodes.name: (i) General estimate
nodes.statement_short: Mean value bound on kernel difference, Lemma 2.3, and choice of small R_1.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg|\\ &\preceq |\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|\bigg(\frac{|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+ \frac{\log|z|}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg) +\frac{|\kappa(x,z)-\kappa(y,z)|}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\ &\preceq \big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\bigg(\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline \alpha(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+ \frac{1+\log|z|}{|z|^{d+\underline \alpha(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg), \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (2.28)
nodes.label: e:pp

nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t,w)\big|\\ &\preceq \!\big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big) \!\cdot\! \begin{cases} (1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ \ &\ |w|\leqslant {1}/{2},\\ \big(1+|\log |w||+(1+|\log t|)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\big)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,w),\ \ &\ |w|>{1}/{2}. \end{cases} \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (2.29)
nodes.label: l1-2-2

nodes.statement:
(ii) Suppose, in addition, that  there are some $y_0\in\mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that
 $\alpha(x)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $x \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then \eqref{e:pp} is reduced to
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
&\bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y_0,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y_0)}}\bigg|\preceq \big(|x-y|^{\beta_0}\wedge
1\big)\cdot\bigg(\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y_0)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}}+ \frac{1}{|z|^{d+
\alpha(y_0)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg)
\end{split}
\end{equation*} for all $x\in B(y_0,r_0)$.
Having this at hand and repeating the same argument above, we can
easily see that the second assertion holds in this case.
nodes.name: (ii) Locally constant α
nodes.statement_short: When α is constant near y_0 the kernel difference has no log factor.

nodes.statement: Let $R_1=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$, where $R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$ is the constant in Lemma \ref{l1-2}. According to Lemma \ref{l1-2}, we only need to treat the case that $|x-y|> R_1$. (1) We first assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. By \eqref{e2-3}, for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$, we have \begin{equation} \begin{split} | {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)| & \preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)|\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &\quad +\int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}} \big(p^y(t,x-y\pm z)+p^y(t,x-y)\big)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &=:J_1+J_2. \end{split} \end{equation} Applying \eqref{p1-1-1} and using the mean value theorem, we can get \begin{align*} J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|\nabla^2 p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y+\theta_{x,y,z}z)||z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\, dz\\ &\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\frac{t}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|x-y+\theta_{x,y, z}z|)^{d+\alpha(y)+2}} |z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\, dz\\ &\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\, dz\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}=\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y), \end{align*} where in the first inequality $\theta_{x,y,z}$ is a constant depending on $x,y,z$ such that $|\theta_{x,y,z}|\leqslant 1$, and the third inequality follows from the fact that $$|x-y+\theta_{x,y,z}z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\geqslant {R_1}/{2} \geqslant C_0 t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\quad\textrm{ for any } z\in \mathds R^d\textrm{ with } |z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}.$$ On the other hand, according to \eqref{p1-1-1-1-0} and \eqref{r1-1-1}, we have \begin{equation} \begin{split} J_2&\preceq \int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz + \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y) \int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}}\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz \preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation} Hence, for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$, $$| {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|\preceq\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).$$ Following the same argument above, we have for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$, \begin{equation} | {\mathcal L}^y p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).\end{equation} Therefore, for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$, \begin{align*} |q_0(t,x,y)|&\leqslant | {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|+| {\mathcal L}^y p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y). \end{align*} By now we have shown the second case in the estimate \eqref{l2-1-2}. From \eqref{l1-2-1b} and \eqref{l2-1-2}, we arrive at \eqref{l2-1-33a} immediately. (2) Now we suppose the general case that $\kappa(x,z)$ may depend on $z$. We still define $J_1$ and $J_2$ by those in \eqref{l2-1-3a}. It is not difficult to verify that \eqref{e:ref1} also holds for this case. On the other hand, according to \eqref{p1-1-2}, it holds that \begin{equation} \begin{split} J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\big[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2)\wedge 1\big]\cdot\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &\quad +\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\big[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2)\wedge 1\big]\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &\preceq\frac{t^{1-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz + \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\int_{\{t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\leqslant |z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\\ &\quad + \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}} \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\big[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2)\wedge 1\big]|z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\\ &\preceq \frac{t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\leqslant \frac{t^{1-(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}. \end{split} \end{equation} Here the second step follows from \begin{equation*} \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y+ z)\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\quad\textrm{ when } |x-y|> R_1\textrm{ and }|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}, \end{equation*} which is due to the fact that for $ |x-y|> R_1$ and $ |z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}$ $$|x-y+ z| \geqslant |x-y|-|z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\geqslant {R_1}/{2}\geqslant C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}.$$ Note also that \eqref{l2-1-4} is still true for this case. Combining all the estimates above, we obtain \begin{align*} |q_0(t,x,y)|&\preceq | {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,x-y)|+| {\mathcal L}^y p^y(t,x-y)| \preceq J_1+J_2+| {\mathcal L}^yp^y(t,x-y)|\preceq t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y), \end{align*} where in the last step we used the fact that $t^{-{\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)}}\leqslant t^{-{\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1}}$ for all $t \in (0,1].$ Thus, the second case of \eqref{l2-1-1} is proved.
nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.5 (upper bounds for q_0)
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to |x-y|>R_1 by Lemma 2.7, then bound L^x p^y and L^y p^y separately via near/far splitting of the jump integral.

nodes.statement:
Let $R_1=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$, where $R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$ is the constant in
Lemma \ref{l1-2}. According to Lemma \ref{l1-2},  we only need to
treat the case that $|x-y|> R_1$.
nodes.name: Reduce to |x-y|>R_1
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 2.7 only |x-y|>R_1 needs treatment.

nodes.statement:
(1)  We first assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.


By \eqref{e2-3}, for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$, we have
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
 | {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|
& \preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)|\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\quad +\int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}} \big(p^y(t,x-y\pm z)+p^y(t,x-y)\big)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Applying \eqref{p1-1-1} and using the mean value theorem, we can get
\begin{align*}
J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|\nabla^2 p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y+\theta_{x,y,z}z)||z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\, dz\\
&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\frac{t}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|x-y+\theta_{x,y, z}z|)^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}
|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\, dz\\
&\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant
{R_1}/{2}\}}|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\, dz\preceq
\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}=\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where in the first inequality $\theta_{x,y,z}$ is a constant depending on
$x,y,z$ such that $|\theta_{x,y,z}|\leqslant 1$, and the third inequality follows
from the fact that $$|x-y+\theta_{x,y,z}z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\geqslant
{R_1}/{2} \geqslant C_0 t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\quad\textrm{ for any } z\in \mathds R^d\textrm{ with } |z|\leqslant
{R_1}/{2}.$$
On the other hand, according to \eqref{p1-1-1-1-0} and \eqref{r1-1-1}, we have
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
J_2&\preceq \int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz +
\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y) \int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}}\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz \preceq  \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Hence, for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$,
$$| {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|\preceq\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).$$


Following the same argument above, we have for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$,
\begin{equation} | {\mathcal L}^y p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).\end{equation}
Therefore, for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$,
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)|&\leqslant | {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|+| {\mathcal L}^y p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|\preceq
\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y).
\end{align*}
By now we have shown the second case in the estimate \eqref{l2-1-2}.
From \eqref{l1-2-1b} and \eqref{l2-1-2}, we arrive at
\eqref{l2-1-33a} immediately.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} | {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)| & \preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)|\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &\quad +\int_{\{|z|>{R_1}/{2}\}} \big(p^y(t,x-y\pm z)+p^y(t,x-y)\big)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &=:J_1+J_2. \end{split}

nodes.statement_short: Use the second-difference bound for J_1, giving the factor t^{1-α_2/α_1}.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\big[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2)\wedge 1\big]\cdot\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &\quad +\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\big[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2)\wedge 1\big]\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &\preceq\frac{t^{1-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz + \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\int_{\{t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\leqslant |z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}|z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\\ &\quad + \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}} \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {R_1}/{2}\}}\big[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2)\wedge 1\big]|z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\\ &\preceq \frac{t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}/{\alpha(y)})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\leqslant \frac{t^{1-(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}. \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (2.33)
nodes.label: l2-1-5

nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item [(1)] Suppose $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Then there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation}\begin{split} |q_0(t,x,y)|&\leqslant \begin{cases} c_1t^{-1-({d}/{\alpha(y)})},\quad & |x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}},\\ \frac{c_1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+ \frac{c_1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}},\quad & |x-y|> t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}} \end{cases}\\ &\leqslant \begin{cases} c_1t^{-1-({d}/{\alpha(y)})},\quad & |x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}},\\ \frac{c_1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}\wedge |x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\quad & |x-y|> t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}. \end{cases}\end{split} \end{equation} \item[(2)] Suppose $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}>({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$. Then there exists a constant $c_2:=c_2(\alpha,\kappa)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y)|\leqslant \begin{cases} c_2t^{-1-({d}/{\alpha(y)})},\quad &|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}},\\ \frac{c_1 t^{1-(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}\wedge |x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\quad & |x-y| > t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}. \end{cases} \end{equation} \end{itemize}

nodes.label: p2-1-1a

nodes.statement: (1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. {\bf Case (a): $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}.$} According to \eqref{l1-2-1a}, we can choose $0<\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$ and adjust the constants properly to get that \begin{equation} \begin{split} |q_0(t,x-y)|&\preceq \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(t,x-y)\preceq t^{-\gamma}|x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot\rho^{y,0}_{0}(t,x-y)\\ &\preceq t^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\preceq t^{-({d}/{\alpha(y)})-1}, \end{split} \end{equation} where in the third inequality we have used the fact that $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha_2}}$, and the fourth inequality follows from $\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$. {\bf Case (b): $|x-y|>t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}.$} By \eqref{e2-3}, it holds that \begin{equation} \begin{split} | {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)|& \preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}}\left| \delta_{p^y}\left(t,x-y;z\right)\right|\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &\quad +\int_{\{|z|> {|x-y|}/{2}\}}\left| \delta_{p^y}\left(t,x-y;z\right)\right|\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &=:J_1+J_2. \end{split} \end{equation} Then, using the mean value theorem, we have \begin{align*} J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}} \left|\nabla^2 p^y(t,x-y+\theta_{x,y,z} z)\right|\cdot |z|^2\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}} \frac{t}{\left(t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}+|x-y+\theta_{x,y,z} z|\right)^{d+\alpha(y)+2}} \cdot |z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\\ &\preceq \frac{t}{\left(t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}+|x-y|\right)^{d+\alpha(y)+2}} \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}} |z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\\ &\preceq \frac{|x-y|^{\alpha(y)}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}\cdot |x-y|^{2-\alpha(x)}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}, \end{align*} where in the first inequality $\theta_{x,y,z}$ is a constant depending on $x,y,z$ such that $|\theta_{x,y,z}|\leqslant 1$, in the second inequality we have used \eqref{p1-1-1}, the third inequality follows from the fact that $|x-y+\theta_{x,y,z} z|\geqslant |x-y|-|z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$, and the fourth inequality is due to the fact that $t\leqslant |x-y|^{\alpha(y)}$. On the other hand, by \eqref{p1-1-2} and the fact that $|z|>{|x-y|}/{2}\geqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}/2$, we have $ \left|\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\right|\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)+\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y),$ and so \begin{align*} J_2&\preceq \int_{\{|z|>{|x-y|}/{2}\}}\!\! \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz + \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y)\int_{\{|z|>{|x-y|}/{2}\}}\!\! \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz=:J_{21}+J_{22}. \end{align*} It holds that \begin{align*} J_{21}&\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}} \int_{\{|z|>{|x-y|}/{2}\}}\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\,dz\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\int \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\,dz\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}, \end{align*} where in the first inequality we have used following fact $$ \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\quad\textrm{ for } |z|>{|x-y|}/{2},$$ and the last inequality follows from \eqref{l3-1-1-00}. Furthermore, it is easy to verify that \begin{align*} J_{22}&\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y) \int_{\{|z|>{|x-y|}/{2}\}}\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\, dz\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)+\alpha(y)}}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}, \end{align*} where in the last inequality we used $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$. Combining all these estimates above, we arrive at $$ \left| {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}.$$ Following the same arguments as above, we also have $$ \left| {\mathcal L}^yp^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}.$$ Hence, \begin{align*} |q_0(t,x,y)|&\preceq \left| {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|+\left| {\mathcal L}^yp^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}, \end{align*} from which we can get \eqref{p2-1-1} immediately. (2) Next we consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$. With the estimate \eqref{l2-1-1} and the condition ${\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}>({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$ at hand, we can follow the same argument as in \eqref{p2-1-2a} to verify the upper bound in \eqref{p2-1-1a} for the case that $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$. When $|x-y|>t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$, we still define $J_1$ and $J_2$ via \eqref{p2-1-2}. By carefully tracking the proof above, we find that the argument for the estimates of $J_2$ in part (1) still works. So it remains to consider upper bound for $J_1$. According to \eqref{p1-1-2}, we have \begin{align*} J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}} \big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot \big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)\big)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\int \big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\cdot \bigg(\int_{\{|z|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}} t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz+\int_{\{|z|> t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}}|z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\bigg)\\ &\preceq t^{1-({\alpha(x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\cdot \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\preceq t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}\cdot \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}, \end{align*} where the second inequality above follows from $$ \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\quad\textrm{ for any }|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}.$$ Combining this with the estimate of $J_2$ in part (1) yields \begin{align*} |q_0(t,x,y)|&\preceq \left| {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|+\left| {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|\preceq t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}\cdot \bigg(\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg), \end{align*} which implies that \eqref{p2-1-1a} holds for every $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$. The proof is complete.

nodes.statement:
(2) Next we consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$.
With the estimate \eqref{l2-1-1} and the condition
${\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}>({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$ at hand, we can follow the same argument as in \eqref{p2-1-2a} to verify the
upper bound in \eqref{p2-1-1a} for the case that $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$.

When $|x-y|>t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$, we still define
$J_1$ and $J_2$ via \eqref{p2-1-2}. By carefully tracking the proof above, we find that the argument for the
estimates of $J_2$ in part (1) still works. So it remains to consider upper bound for
$J_1$.
According to \eqref{p1-1-2}, we have
\begin{align*}
J_1&\preceq \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}}
\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot
\big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)\big)\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\int
\big[\big(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\big)\wedge 1\big] \cdot
\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
&\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\cdot \bigg(\int_{\{|z|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}}
t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^{2-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz+\int_{\{|z|> t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\}}|z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz\bigg)\\
&\preceq t^{1-({\alpha(x)}/{\alpha(y)})}\cdot \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\preceq t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}\cdot \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}},
\end{align*}
where the second inequality above follows from
$$ \rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y\pm z)\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\quad\textrm{ for any }|z|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}.$$
Combining this with the estimate of $J_2$ in part (1) yields
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)|&\preceq
\left| {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|+\left| {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,\cdot)(x-y)\right|\preceq t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}\cdot \bigg(\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg),
\end{align*}
which implies that \eqref{p2-1-1a} holds for every $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}$. The proof is complete.

nodes.statement_short: Modify the J_1 estimate via the second-difference bound.

nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\kappa(x,z)=\kappa (x) $ is independent of $z$, then for any $\gamma,\theta>0$ with $\gamma<\theta<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$ and any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa, \gamma, \theta,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $(t,x,x',y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} &|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\ &\leqslant c_1\left(|x-x'|^{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}\wedge 1\right)\\ &\quad \times\Big[\left(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\right)(t,x-y) +\left(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\\ &\qquad\quad +|x-y|^{\varepsilon}\mathds 1_{\{|x-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}(t,x-y) +|x'-y|^{\varepsilon}\mathds 1_{\{|x'-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{split} \end{equation} \item[(2)] For general $\kappa (x, z)$, if $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, then for any $\gamma,\theta>0$ such that $ ({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1+\gamma =:\gamma_2 <\theta<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_2:=c_2(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,\theta,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $(t,x,x',y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} & |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\ &\leqslant c_2\left(|x-x'|^{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}\wedge 1\right) \Big[\left(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma_2 }+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma_2-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\right)(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad\quad +\left(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma_2}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma_2 -({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y) +|x-y|^{\varepsilon}\mathds 1_{\{|x-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma_2 }(t,x-y)\\ & \qquad \quad +|x'-y|^{\varepsilon}\mathds 1_{\{|x'-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma_2 }(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{split} \end{equation} \end{itemize}

The proof is split into the following five different cases. { f Case (a): $|x-x'|>R_1$.} By \eqref{l2-1-2} and the condition $ eta_0>\alpha_2	heta$, it holds that  egin{align*} |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)| &\leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)|+|q_0(t,x',y)|\preceq ho_{-\gamma}^{y, eta_0}(t,x-y)+ho_{-\gamma}^{y, eta_0}(t,x'-y)\ &\preceq  ig(|x-x'|^{{\alpha_1( eta_0-\alpha_2	heta)/{\alpha(x)}}}\wedge1 ig) ig(ho_{-\gamma}^{y, eta_0}(t,x-y)+ho_{-\gamma}^{y, eta_0}(t,x'-y) ig).\end{align*} { f Case (b): $C_0t^{1/\alpha(y)}\leqslant |x-x'|\leqslant R_1$ for some small constant $C_0>0$.} According to \eqref{l2-1-2} again, we have  egin{align*} |q_0(t,x,y)|\preceq& ho_{-\gamma}^{y, eta_0}(t,x-y)\preceq t^{{( eta_0-\alpha(x)	heta)}/{\alpha(x)}} ho_{-\gamma+	heta-({ eta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y, eta_0}(t,x-y) \ \preceq&|x-x'|^{{{\alpha(y)( eta_0-\alpha(x)	heta)}/{\alpha(x)}}} ho_{-\gamma+	heta-({ eta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y, eta_0}(t,x-y) \ \preceq&|x-x'|^{{\alpha_1( eta_0-\alpha_2	heta)/{\alpha(x)}}} ho_{-\gamma+	heta-({ eta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y, eta_0}(t,x-y), \end{align*} where the third inequality is due to $t\preceq |x-x'|^{\alpha(y)}$. abla^3 p^y(t,x'+	heta''(x-x')+	heta'	heta z) (x-x',	heta z, z)\,d	heta''d	heta'\,d	heta,\end{align*} which implies that  egin{align*} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x';z) | &\leqslant \Big(\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1\int_0^1 |
