By the estimates for $J_{11}$, $J_{12}$, $J_{21}$ and $J_{22}$, we know that for every $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ and $|x-y|>R_1$,  egin{align*} |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)| \preceq& |x-x'|\cdot ig[ ho^{y, eta_0}_{-\gamma_2-({1/\alpha(y)})}(t,x-y) +ho^{y, eta_0}_{-\gamma_2-({1/\alpha(y)})}(t,x'-y) ig]\ &+|x-x'|^{ eta_0} ig(1+\log(1+|x'-y|) ig)ho^{y,0}_{-\gamma_2}(t,x'-y). \end{align*} Combining the estimates above for all the cases, we can find a constant $C_0>0$ small enough such that for every $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0 t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ and $\gamma,\varepsilon>0$,  egin{align*} |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\preceq& |x-x'|\cdot ig[ ho^{y, eta_0}_{-\gamma_2 -({1/\alpha(y)})}(t,x-y) +ho^{y, eta_0}_{-\gamma_2 -({1/\alpha(y)})}(t,x'-y) ig]\ &+|x-x'|^{ eta_0}|x-y|^{\varepsilon}\mathds 1_{\{|x-y|>R_0\}}ho^{y,0}_{-\gamma_2}(t,x-y)\ &+|x-x'|^{ eta_0}|x'-y|^{\varepsilon}\mathds 1_{\{|x'-y|>R_0\}}ho^{y,0}_{-\gamma_2}(t,x'-y). \end{align*} Then, by the same argument for \eqref{p3-1-6} and all the conclusions above, we can immediately show that \eqref{p3-1-2a-1} holds.
nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.9 (Hölder continuity of q_0)
nodes.statement_short: Five-case analysis on |x-x'| and |x-y| relative to t^{1/α(y)} and R_1, controlling differences of second differences of p^y and of the jump kernels. Key step: the third-derivative bound for p^y far from the singularity.

nodes.statement: In the remainder of this paper, we denote $\nabla p^y(t,\cdot)(x)$ by $\nabla p^y(t,x)$ for simplicity.
nodes.name: Notation for ∇p^y
nodes.statement_short: Abbreviate ∇p^y(t,·)(x) as ∇p^y(t,x).

nodes.name: (1) κ independent of z
nodes.statement_short: Five-case analysis yielding the Hölder estimate for q_0.

nodes.name: Case (a): |x-x'|>R_1
nodes.statement_short: Trivial from the upper bound for q_0.

nodes.statement:
{\bf Case (b): $C_0t^{1/\alpha(y)}\leqslant |x-x'|\leqslant R_1$ for some small
constant $C_0>0$.}


According to \eqref{l2-1-2} again, we have
\begin{align*} |q_0(t,x,y)|\preceq& \rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y)\preceq t^{{(\beta_0-\alpha(x)\theta)}/{\alpha(x)}} \rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y) \\
\preceq&|x-x'|^{{{\alpha(y)(\beta_0-\alpha(x)\theta)}/{\alpha(x)}}} \rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y) \\
\preceq&|x-x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}} \rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y),  \end{align*}
where the third inequality is due to $t\preceq |x-x'|^{\alpha(y)}$.
Then
\begin{align*}&|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\
&\leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)|+|q_0(t,x',y)|\\
&\preceq |x-\!x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}} \! \rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y)  +
|x-\!x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x')}}}\!
\rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x'\!-y)\\
&\preceq |x-\!x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}}\Big(
\rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x\!-y)+
\rho_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x'\!-y)\Big).\end{align*}
Here in the last inequality we have used the fact that for $ x,x'\in
\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1,$
\begin{equation} |x-x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x')}}}\preceq
|x-x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}},
\end{equation}
which can be verified by following the argument of \eqref{l3-1-1a}.
nodes.name: Case (b): C_0t^{1/α(y)}≤|x-x'|≤R_1
nodes.statement_short: Use t ⪯ |x-x'|^{α(y)} in the upper bound.

nodes.statement: |x-x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x')}}}\preceq |x-x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}},
nodes.name: Equation (2.40)
nodes.label: p3-1-3

nodes.statement:
Next, we mainly treat the case that $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{1/\alpha(y)}$,
which we divide into three cases.
nodes.name: Remaining small-increment cases
nodes.statement_short: Divide |x-x'|≤C_0t^{1/α(y)} into three cases.

nodes.statement:
{\bf Case (c): $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{1/\alpha(y)}$ and $|x-y|\geqslant R_1$.}

By the definition of $q_0(t,x,y)$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
 |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|
&=\frac{1}{2}\bigg|\int_{\mathds R^d} \delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\bigg(\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg)\,dz\\
&\qquad\quad-\int_{\mathds R^d} \delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)\bigg(\frac{\kappa(x',z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x')}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg)\,dz\bigg|\\
&\leqslant \frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathds R^d} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg|\,dz\\
&\quad+ \frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathds R^d} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x',z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x')}}-\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}} \bigg|\,dz\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{split}
\end{equation}


Note that \begin{equation} \begin{split} \delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)=&p^y(t,x+z)+p^y(t,x-z)-2p^y(t,x)\\
=&\int_0^1 \frac{d}{d\theta}\Big(p^y(t,x+\theta z)+p^y(t,x-\theta z)\Big)\,d\theta\\
=&\int_0^1 \langle \nabla p^y(t,x+\theta z)-\nabla p^y(t,x-\theta z),z\rangle \,d\theta\\
=&\int_0^1 \Big\langle \int_{-1}^1 \frac{d}{d \theta'}\left(\nabla p^y(t,x+\theta'\theta z)\right)d\theta',z \Big\rangle \,d\theta\\
=&\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1 \nabla^2 p^y(t,x+\theta'\theta z)(\theta z, z)d\theta'\,d\theta,\end{split}\end{equation}
and so
\begin{align*}  \delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x';z)
&=\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1 \big(\nabla^2 p^y(t,x+\theta'\theta z)- \nabla^2 p^y(t,x'+\theta'\theta z)\big)(\theta z, z)\,d\theta'\,d\theta\\
&=\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1\int_0^1  \frac{d}{d\theta''}\Big(\nabla^2 p^y(t,x'+\theta''(x-x')+\theta'\theta z)\Big)
(\theta z, z)\,d\theta''d\theta'\,d\theta\\
&=\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1\int_0^1  \nabla^3 p^y(t,x'+\theta''(x-x')+\theta'\theta z)
(x-x',\theta z, z)\,d\theta''d\theta'\,d\theta,\end{align*} which implies that
\begin{align*}
 |\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x';z) |
&\leqslant \Big(\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1\int_0^1 |\nabla^3 p^y(t,x'+\theta''(x-x')+\theta'\theta z)|\,\,d\theta''d\theta'\,d\theta\Big)
\cdot |z|^2|x-x'|.
\end{align*}
For every $x,x',z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0 t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, $|x|\geqslant cR_1$, $|x'|\geqslant cR_1$ and $|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}$
for $C_0$ small enough, there exists a constant $c'>0$ such that for every $\theta\in(0,1)$, $\theta'\in(-1,1)$ and $\theta''\in(0,1)$, we have
$|x'+\theta''(x-x')+\theta'\theta z|\geqslant c'|x'|\geqslant c''R_1,$ which along with \eqref{p1-1-1} yields that
$$|\nabla^3 p^y(t,x'+\theta''(x-x')+\theta'\theta z)| \preceq \frac{t}{|x'|^{d+\alpha(y)+3}}.$$ Combining with all the estimates above, we arrive at that
for $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{1/\alpha(y)}$, $|x|\geqslant cR_1$, $|x'|\geqslant cR_1$ and $|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}$,
\begin{equation} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x';z) |\preceq \frac{t|z|^2|x-x'|}{|x'|^{d+\alpha(y)+3}}.
   \end{equation}


Since $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\leqslant C_0$, $|x'-y|\geqslant cR_1$ holds for some constant $c>0$.
By taking $x=x-y$ and $x'=x'-y$ in \eqref{e:conpr1}, we obtain that for all $z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}$,
\begin{equation} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z) |\preceq \frac{t|z|^2|x-x'|}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+3}}.  \end{equation}

Let \begin{equation} \begin{split}
J_1=&\frac{1}{2}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg|\,dz\\
&+ \frac{1}{2}\int_{\{|z|> {cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg|\,dz\\
=&:J_{11}+J_{12}.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
 By \eqref{e:conpr2},
 \begin{align*}J_{11}\preceq &|x-x'|\frac{t}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+3}} \int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}}\bigg( \frac{|z|^2}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{|z|^2}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg)\,dz\\
 \preceq& |x-x'|\frac{t}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+3}} \preceq |x-x'|\frac{1}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},
 \end{align*} where the last inequality is due to $|x'-y|>cR_1$ and $t\leqslant 1$.
On the other hand, according to \eqref{r1-1-1}, we have for any $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\int_{\{|z|>{cR_1}/{4}\}} \rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z) \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha (x)}}\,dz \preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\\
&\int_{\{|z|>{cR_1}/{4}\}} \rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y) \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha (x)}}\,dz \preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{p1-1-4} with \eqref{l3-1-3b} and the fact that $|z|>{cR_1}/{4}$ implies $|z|>C_1t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, we arrive at
\begin{align*}
J_{12}&\preceq t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|x-x'| \int_{\{|z|>{cR_1}/{4}\}}\Big(\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\
&\qquad \qquad\qquad\qquad +\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'-y)\Big)
\bigg(\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg)\,dz\\
&\preceq t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|x-x'| \left( \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}+
\frac{1}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha_1}} \right). \end{align*} By both of the
estimates above, we obtain that
 \begin{align*}J_1&\preceq t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|x-x'| \big( \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)+\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x'-y)\big)\preceq  |x-x'| \big( \rho_{-{1/\alpha(y)}}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y)+\rho_{-{1/\alpha(y)}}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x'-y)\big), \end{align*}
where the last inequality follows from the facts that $|x-y|\geqslant cR_1$ and $|x'-y|\geqslant c R_1$.


Let \begin{equation} \begin{split}
J_2=&\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x',z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x')}}-\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}} \bigg|\,dz\\
&+ \int_{\{|z|> {cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x',z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x')}}-\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}} \bigg|\,dz\\
=&:J_{21}+J_{22}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Since $|x'-y|>cR_1$, by \eqref{e:conpr0} and \eqref{p1-1-1}, we find that for any $|z|<{cR_1}/{4} $,
\begin{align*}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)|&\leqslant |z|^2\int_0^1\int_{-1}^1 |\nabla^2 p^y(t,x'-y+\theta'\theta z)|\,d\theta'\,d\theta \preceq |z|^2 \frac{ t}{ |x'-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}.\end{align*}
 Thus,
 due to \eqref{e:pp},
 \begin{align*}J_{21} \preceq& |x-x'|^{\beta_0} \frac{t}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha(y)+2}}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}} \!\!\frac{1+|\log |z||}{|z|^{d+\overline\alpha(x;x')}}|z|^2\,dz
 \preceq  |x-x'|^{\beta_0} \frac{1}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\end{align*} where we have used the facts that $|x'-y|>cR_1$ and $t<1$ in the second inequality.
On the other hand, when $|z|> {cR_1}/{4}$,
$$|\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)|\preceq p^y(t,x'-y\pm z)+p^y(t,x'-y).$$
Having this at hand and using \eqref{r1-1-2} and \eqref{p1-1-1-1-0}, we know that
$$\int_{\{|z|>{cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)|\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(x;x')}}\,dz
\preceq \frac{\log(1+|x'-y|)}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}.$$
Then, by \eqref{e:pp}, we find that
\begin{align*}
J_{22}&\preceq |x-x'|^{\beta_0}\cdot \int_{\{|z|>{cR_1}/{4}\}}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)|\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(x;x')}}\,dz  \preceq   |x-x'|^{\beta_0}\frac{\log(1+|x'-y|)}{|x'-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}.
\end{align*}
By the estimates for $J_{21}$ and $J_{22}$, we have
\begin{equation*}
J_2\preceq |x-x'|^{\beta_0}\log(1+|x'-y|)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x'-y).
\end{equation*}

Putting the estimates of $J_1$ and $J_2$ together, we finally arrive at
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\preceq & |x-x'|\big( \rho_{-{1/\alpha(y)}}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y)+\rho_{-{1/\alpha(y)}}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x'-y)\big)\\
&+|x-x'|^{\beta_0}\log(1+|x'-y|)\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x'-y).
\end{align*}
nodes.name: Case (c): |x-y|≥R_1
nodes.statement_short: Third-derivative bound of p^y far from the singularity controls J_1 and J_2.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)| &=\frac{1}{2}\bigg|\int_{\mathds R^d} \delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\bigg(\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg)\,dz\\ &\qquad\quad-\int_{\mathds R^d} \delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)\bigg(\frac{\kappa(x',z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x')}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg)\,dz\bigg|\\ &\leqslant \frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathds R^d} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg|\,dz\\ &\quad+ \frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathds R^d} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x',z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x')}}-\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}} \bigg|\,dz\\ &=:J_1+J_2. \end{split}

abla p^y(t,x+	heta z)-

nodes.name: Equation (2.42)
nodes.label: e:conpr0

nodes.statement: |\delta_{p^y}(t,x;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x';z) |\preceq \frac{t|z|^2|x-x'|}{|x'|^{d+\alpha(y)+3}}.
nodes.name: Equation (2.43)
nodes.label: e:conpr1

nodes.name: Equation (2.44)
nodes.label: e:conpr2

nodes.statement: \begin{split} J_1=&\frac{1}{2}\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg|\,dz\\ &+ \frac{1}{2}\int_{\{|z|> {cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}-\frac{\kappa(y,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}} \bigg|\,dz\\ =&:J_{11}+J_{12}. \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (2.45)
nodes.label: p3-1-3a

nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\int_{\{|z|>{cR_1}/{4}\}} \rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z) \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha (x)}}\,dz \preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\\ &\int_{\{|z|>{cR_1}/{4}\}} \rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y) \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha (x)}}\,dz \preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}. \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (2.46)
nodes.label: l3-1-3b

nodes.statement: \begin{split} J_2=&\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x',z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x')}}-\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}} \bigg|\,dz\\ &+ \int_{\{|z|> {cR_1}/{4}\}} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x'-y;z)| \bigg|\frac{\kappa(x',z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x')}}-\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}} \bigg|\,dz\\ =&:J_{21}+J_{22}. \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (2.47)
nodes.label: p3-1-4a

nodes.name: Case (d): t^{1/α(y)}≤|x-y|<R_1
nodes.statement_short: Combine Hölder bounds of δ_{p^y} with Lemma 2.3-type integrals.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} & \int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]\big (\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)\big)\\ &\qquad\qquad \times \bigg(\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}} +\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(y;x)}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg)\,dz\\ &\preceq \left(1+|\log t|\right)t^{-{(\overline{\alpha}(y;x)-\alpha(y))}/{\alpha(y)}} \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)\preceq \rho_{-\gamma}^{y,0}(t,x-y), \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (2.48)
nodes.label: p3-1-4

nodes.statement: \begin{split} J_2 & \preceq |x-x'|^{\beta_0}\int_{\mathds R^d}\left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]\cdot\Big( \rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'\!-y)\!+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'\!-y\pm z)\Big)\\ & \qquad\times \bigg(\frac{|\log|z||+1}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(x;x')}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}} \!+\frac{|\log|z||+1}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(x;x')}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\!\!\bigg)\,dz. \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (2.49)
nodes.label: p3-1-5a

nodes.statement: \begin{split} & \int_{\mathds R^d}\left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]\cdot\big( \rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'-y\pm z)\big)\\ &\qquad \qquad\qquad \qquad\qquad \times \bigg(\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(x;x')}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|\leqslant 1\}} +\frac{1+|\log|z||}{|z|^{d+\underline{\alpha}(x;x')}}\mathds 1_{\{|z|> 1\}}\bigg)\,dz\\ & \preceq \left(1+|\log t|\right)t^{1-({\overline{\alpha}(x;x')}/{\alpha(y)})}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x'-y). \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (2.50)
nodes.label: p3-1-5

nodes.name: Case (e): |x-y|≤t^{1/α(y)}
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the argument of Case (d) near the diagonal.

nodes.name: Combine the cases
nodes.statement_short: Convert powers of |x-x'| into the claimed Hölder exponent and conclude part (1).

nodes.statement: \begin{split} & |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)| \\ & \preceq |x-x'|^{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}} \Big( \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}(t,x-y) +\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma+\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}(t,x'-y)\\ &\qquad +\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}(t,x'-y)+|x'-y|^{\varepsilon}\mathds 1_{\{|x'-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}(t,x'-y)\Big). \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (2.51)
nodes.label: p3-1-6

nodes.statement:
(2) Now we study the estimate for $|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|$ under the assumption that
$\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$.
Recall that, by  \eqref{l2-1-1}, we have
\begin{equation} |q_0(t,x,y)|\preceq \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2 }(t,x-y),\quad (t,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d,
\end{equation}
where $\gamma_2 =:\gamma+({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$.

Using \eqref{p3-1-8} and following the arguments in {\bf Case (a)} and {\bf Case (b)} of  part (1) above, we derive that for every $(t,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$ such that
$|x-x'|\geqslant C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ (which includes both $|x-x'|>R_1$
and $C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\leqslant |x-x'|\leqslant R_1$, and where as in (1) the constant $C_0$ is chosen to be small enough) and $\gamma_2 <\theta<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$,
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|& \preceq
\big(|x-x'|^{\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}}\wedge 1\big)\\
&\quad\times\big(\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2 +\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}(t,x-y)
+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2 +\theta-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}(t,x'-y)\big).
\end{align*}

Note that
in the proofs of {\bf Case (d)} and {\bf Case (e)} above, we do not need the assumption that
$\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, so the conclusions there are still true, which in particular means that
\eqref{p3-1-2a-1} holds for {\bf Case (d)} and {\bf Case (e)}.
Now we turn to the case that $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ and $|x-y|>R_1$, i.e., the {\bf Case (c)} above.
We still define
$J_{11}$, $J_{12}$, $J_{21}$ and $J_{22}$ as those in \eqref{p3-1-2aa}, \eqref{p3-1-3a} and \eqref{p3-1-4a}, respectively.


For $J_{11}$, we apply \eqref{p1-1-4} instead of \eqref{e:conpr2} in part (1), and derive that
\begin{align*}
J_{11}\preceq \,&t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|x-x'|\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}}
[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}} |z|^2)\wedge 1]\\
&\times\Big(
\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x'-y\pm z)\Big)\cdot\bigg(\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}
+\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg)\,dz.
\end{align*}
Note that $|x-y|>R_1$. By \eqref{r1-1-1a}, we arrive at
\begin{align*}
&\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}}[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}} |z|^2)\wedge 1]
\big(
\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y)
+\rho_1^{y,0}(t,x-y\pm z)\big) \bigg(\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}
+\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg)\,dz\preceq \frac{t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},
\end{align*}
which yields that
\begin{equation*}
J_{11}\preceq\, |x-x'|\big(\rho_{-\gamma_2-({1/\alpha(y)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y)
+\rho_{-\gamma_2-({1/\alpha(y)})}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x'-y)\big).
\end{equation*}
Similarly, using \eqref{p1-1-2} instead of \eqref{p1-1-1} in the estimate of $J_{21}$ and applying
\eqref{r1-1-2a}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
J_{21} &\preceq |x-x'|^{\beta_0}\cdot \bigg(
\int_{\{|z|\leqslant {cR_1}/{4}\}}[(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}} |z|^2)\wedge 1]
\big[\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x'-y\pm z)+\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x'-y)\big]
\frac{1+|\log |z||}{|z|^{d+\overline{\alpha}(x;x')}}\,dz\bigg)\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{\beta_0}(1+|\log t|+|\log|x'-y||)\rho_{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}^{y,0}(t,x'-y).
\end{align*}
As explained before, the proofs for estimates of $J_{12}$ and
$J_{22}$ in (1) do not require the condition that $\kappa(x,z)$ is
independent of $z$, so those estimates still hold here.

By the estimates for $J_{11}$, $J_{12}$, $J_{21}$ and $J_{22}$, we know that for
every $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ and $|x-y|>R_1$,
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|
 \preceq& |x-x'|\cdot\big[
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2-({1/\alpha(y)})}(t,x-y)
+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2-({1/\alpha(y)})}(t,x'-y)\big]\\
&+|x-x'|^{\beta_0}\big(1+\log(1+|x'-y|)\big)\rho^{y,0}_{-\gamma_2}(t,x'-y).
\end{align*}
Combining the estimates above for all the cases, we can find a constant $C_0>0$ small enough such that for
every $|x-x'|\leqslant C_0 t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ and
$\gamma,\varepsilon>0$,
\begin{align*}
|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\preceq& |x-x'|\cdot\big[
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2 -({1/\alpha(y)})}(t,x-y)
+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2 -({1/\alpha(y)})}(t,x'-y)\big]\\
&+|x-x'|^{\beta_0}|x-y|^{\varepsilon}\mathds 1_{\{|x-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{-\gamma_2}(t,x-y)\\
&+|x-x'|^{\beta_0}|x'-y|^{\varepsilon}\mathds 1_{\{|x'-y|>R_0\}}\rho^{y,0}_{-\gamma_2}(t,x'-y).
\end{align*}
Then, by the same argument for \eqref{p3-1-6} and all the conclusions above, we can immediately show that \eqref{p3-1-2a-1} holds.
nodes.name: (2) General κ
nodes.statement_short: Adapt the five cases with γ_2 in place of γ, using the second-difference bounds.

nodes.statement: |q_0(t,x,y)|\preceq \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma_2 }(t,x-y),\quad (t,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d,
nodes.name: Equation (2.52)
nodes.label: p3-1-8

nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] For every $\theta_1,\theta_2\in \mathds R$ and $\beta_1,\beta_2 \in (0,1)$, it holds for all $0<s<t\leqslant 1$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ that \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\preceq \Big[(t-s)^{\theta_1+[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\alpha(x)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2} \big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha(x)\}}\big)\\ &\qquad+(t-s)^{\theta_1} s^{\theta_2 +[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1]-1}\big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\Big]\rho_{0}^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad +(t-s)^{\theta_1+[({\beta_1}/{\alpha(x)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2} \big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1=\alpha(x)\}}\big)\rho_{0}^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad+(t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2+({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1 -1} \big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation} \item[(2)] For every $\theta_1,\theta_2\in \mathds R$ and $\beta_1,\beta_2 \in (0,1)$, it holds for every $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ and $0<s<t\leqslant 1$ that \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\preceq \Big[(t-s)^{\theta_1+[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\alpha_2})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2}\big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha_2\}}\big)\\ &\quad+(t-s)^{\theta_1} s^{\theta_2 +[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\alpha_2})\wedge 1]-1}\big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha_2\}}\big)\Big]\rho_{0}^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\quad +(t-s)^{\theta_1+[({\beta_1}/{\alpha_2})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2}\big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1=\alpha_2\}}\big)\rho_{0}^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y)\\ &\quad+(t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2+[({\beta_2}/{\alpha_2})\wedge 1] -1}\big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_2=\alpha_2\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation}\end{itemize}
nodes.name: Lemma 3.1 (convolution inequality with variable index)
nodes.statement_short: Space convolution of ρ_{θ_1}^{z,β_1}(t-s,x-z) and ρ_{θ_2}^{y,β_2}(s,z-y) is bounded by explicit powers of t-s and s times ρ_0^{y,·}(t,x-y).
nodes.label: l3-2

nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\preceq \Big[(t-s)^{\theta_1+[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\alpha(x)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2} \big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha(x)\}}\big)\\ &\qquad+(t-s)^{\theta_1} s^{\theta_2 +[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1]-1}\big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\Big]\rho_{0}^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad +(t-s)^{\theta_1+[({\beta_1}/{\alpha(x)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2} \big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1=\alpha(x)\}}\big)\rho_{0}^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad+(t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2+({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1 -1} \big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y). \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (3.1)
nodes.label: l3-2-0

nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\preceq \Big[(t-s)^{\theta_1+[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\alpha_2})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2}\big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha_2\}}\big)\\ &\quad+(t-s)^{\theta_1} s^{\theta_2 +[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\alpha_2})\wedge 1]-1}\big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha_2\}}\big)\Big]\rho_{0}^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\quad +(t-s)^{\theta_1+[({\beta_1}/{\alpha_2})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2}\big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1=\alpha_2\}}\big)\rho_{0}^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y)\\ &\quad+(t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2+[({\beta_2}/{\alpha_2})\wedge 1] -1}\big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_2=\alpha_2\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y). \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (3.2)
nodes.label: l3-2-1

nodes.statement: (1) The proof is split into three cases. {\bf Case (a): $|x-y|>2.$} It holds that \begin{equation} \begin{split} \int_{\mathds R^d} \rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz &\leqslant \int_{\{|z-y|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}} \rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz\\ &\quad+\int_{\{|z-y|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}} \rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &=:J_1+J_2. \end{split} \end{equation} If $|z-y|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\geqslant 1\geqslant s^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, then \begin{equation} \begin{split} \rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)&\preceq \frac{1}{|z-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation} Observe that (see e.g.\ the proof of \cite[Lemma 2.2]{CZ}) for any $x,y, z\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big(|x-z|^{\beta_1}\wedge 1\big) \big(|z-y|^{\beta_2}\wedge 1\big)\leqslant &\big(|x-z|^{\beta_1+\beta_2}\wedge 1\big) +\big(|x-z|^{\beta_1}\wedge 1\big) \big(|x-y|^{\beta_2}\wedge 1\big). \end{split} \end{equation} Combining this with \eqref{l3-2-2} and the first inequality in \eqref{l3-1-1}, we get that for $\beta_1,\beta_2\in (0,1)$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} J_1&\preceq (t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,\beta_1+\beta_2}_0(t-s,x-z)\,dz\\ &\quad +(t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y)\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,\beta_1}_0(t-s,x-z)\,dz\\ &\preceq (t-s)^{\theta_1+[(({\beta_1+\beta_2})/{\alpha(x) })\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2}\big(1\!+\!|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha(x)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\quad+ (t-s)^{[\theta_1+({\beta_1}/{\alpha(x)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2}\big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1=\alpha(x)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation} If $|z-y|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$, then $|x-z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\geqslant 1 \geqslant (t-s)^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}$, and so \begin{align*} & \rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)\preceq \frac{1}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y). \end{align*} Combining this with \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big(|x-z|^{\beta_1}\wedge 1\big) \big(|z-y|^{\beta_2}\wedge 1\big)\leqslant &\big(|z-y|^{\beta_1+\beta_2}\wedge 1\big) +\big(|z-y|^{\beta_2}\wedge 1\big) \big(|x-y|^{\beta_1}\wedge 1\big), \end{split} \end{equation} we arrive at \begin{equation} \begin{split} J_2&\preceq (t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,\beta_1+\beta_2}_0(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\quad +(t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y)\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,\beta_2}_0(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\preceq (t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2+[(({\beta_1+\beta_2})/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1]-1} \big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\quad+ (t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2+[({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1]-1}\big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y), \end{split} \end{equation} where the second inequality follows from the first inequality in \eqref{l3-1-1-00}. According to the above estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, \eqref{l3-2-1} holds in this case. {\bf Case (b): $2t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}\leqslant |x-y|\leqslant 2$.} Let $J_1$ and $J_2$ be defined by \eqref{l3-2-1a}. If $|z-y|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$ and $0<s<t<1$, then $|z-y|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$, and so \begin{equation} \begin{split} \rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)&\preceq \begin{cases} |z-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},& |z-y|\leqslant 1,\\ |z-y|^{-d-\alpha_1},& |z-y|>1 \end{cases} \\ &\preceq \begin{cases} |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},&|z-y|\leqslant 1,\\ |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1},& |z-y|>1 \end{cases} \\ &\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y), \end{split} \end{equation} where in the third inequality we have used the fact that $$|x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\quad \textrm{ for all }|x-y|\leqslant 2 ,$$ and the last inequality follows from $$|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)} \preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\quad\textrm{ for all } |x-y|\geqslant 2t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}\geqslant 2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}.$$ Using \eqref{l3-2-6} and following the same argument of \eqref{l3-2-4}, we know that \eqref{l3-2-4} is satisfied too. If $|z-y|<{|x-y|}/{2}$, then $|x-z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$, and so we obtain \begin{equation} \begin{split} \rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)&\preceq \begin{cases} |x-z|^{-d-\alpha(z)},& |x-z|\leqslant 1,\\ |x-z|^{-d-\alpha_1}, & |x-z|>1 \end{cases} \\ &\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(z)} \preceq |x-y|^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)}\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\ &\preceq |x-y|^{-|\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)|}\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\ &\preceq |x-y|^{-C|x-y|^{\beta_0}}\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\ &\preceq \exp\big(C|\log|x-y||\cdot|x-y|^{\beta_0}\big)\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\ &\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y), \end{split} \end{equation} where in the second inequality we used the fact that if $|x-z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$ and $|x-y|\leqslant 2$, then $|x-z|^{-d-\alpha_1}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(z)},$ the fifth inequality follows from the fact that $$|\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)|\preceq |z-y|^{\beta_0}\leqslant C |x-y|^{\beta_0}\quad\textrm{ for all }|z-y|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2},$$ in the seventh inequality we used $$\sup_{z\in \mathds R^d: |z|\leqslant 2}\exp\big(C|\log |z||\cdot|z|^{\beta_0}\big)<\infty,$$ and the last inequality is due to the same argument of the last one in \eqref{l3-2-6}. Using the above inequality for $\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)$ and following the same procedure of \eqref{l3-2-5a}, we know that \eqref{l3-2-5a} still holds. Therefore, according to the estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, \eqref{l3-2-1} also holds in this case. {\bf Case (c): $|x-y|\leqslant 2t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}$.} Note that for any $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} 1\leqslant& \frac{t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}}{t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}}\leqslant t^{-\frac{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})-\alpha(y)}{\alpha(y)\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}} \leqslant t^{-\frac{Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant \exp\big(C|\log t|\cdot t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}} \big)\leqslant C_1 , \end{split} \end{equation} hence $|x-y|\leqslant 2t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}$ implies that $|x-y|\leqslant C_2 t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ for some constant $C_2>0$. On the other hand, \begin{align*} \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz &\leqslant \int_{\{|z-y|> t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}\rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz\\ &\quad+\int_{\{|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}\rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &=:J_1+J_2. \end{align*} If $|z-y|\geqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}>s^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, then \begin{align*} \rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)\preceq |z-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq t^{-({d+\alpha(y)})/{\alpha(y)}}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y), \end{align*} where the second inequality follows from $|z-y|\geqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, and the last inequality is due to $t^{-({d+\alpha(y)})/{\alpha(y)}}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)$ for all $|x-y|\leqslant C_2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$. Applying the above estimate for $\rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)$ and following the same argument of \eqref{l3-2-4}, we can find that \eqref{l3-2-4} still holds for $J_1$ here. Now we turn to estimate for $J_2$, which is divided into the following two subcases: {\bf Subcase (c1): $s>{t}/{2}$.} If $|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, then \begin{align*} \rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)&\preceq s^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y), \end{align*} where the second inequality follows from $s>{t}/{2}$, and in the last inequality we have used the fact that $t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)$ for all $|x-y|\leqslant C_2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$. Having the above estimate for $\rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)$ at hand, we also can follow the same procedure of \eqref{l3-2-4} to get that \begin{align*} J_2&\preceq (t-s)^{\theta_1+(({\beta_1+\beta_2})/{\alpha(x)})-1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)+ (t-s)^{\theta_1+({\beta_1}/{\alpha(x)})-1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y). \end{align*} {\bf Subcase (c2): $s\leqslant {t}/{2}$.} If $|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, then we have \begin{align*} \rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)&\preceq (t-s)^{-({d}/{\alpha(z)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d}/{\alpha(z)})-1}\preceq t^{-|({d}/{\alpha(z)})-({d/\alpha(y)})|}\cdot t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\\ &\preceq t^{-Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}\cdot t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y), \end{align*} where the second inequality is due to $(t-s)\geqslant {t}/{2}$, in the fourth inequality we used the fact that $|\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)|\preceq |z-y|^{\beta_0}\preceq t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha(y)}}\preceq t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}},$ the fifth inequality follows from $$\sup_{t \in (0,1]}t^{-Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}\preceq \sup_{t \in (0,1]} \exp\big(C|\log t|t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}\big)<\infty,$$ and the last inequality is again due to the fact that $t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)$ for all $|x-y|\leqslant C_2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$. Using the above estimate for $\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)$ and following the same procedure of \eqref{l3-2-5a}, we can also get \eqref{l3-2-5a}. Combining both estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we know \eqref{l3-2-1} holds for {\bf Case (c)}. Therefore, the proof of \eqref{l3-2-0} is complete. (2) We can apply the second inequality in \eqref{l3-1-1} in the proofs of \eqref{l3-2-4} and \eqref{l3-2-5a}, and follow the same arguments as above to prove \eqref{l3-2-1}.
nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1 (convolution inequality with variable index)
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on |x-y| (>2, intermediate, near-diagonal), splitting the convolution at |z-y|=|x-y|/2 and using Hölder continuity of α to compare indices.

nodes.name: (1) Variable-index convolution inequality
nodes.statement_short: Prove the first inequality by three cases on |x-y|.

nodes.name: Case (a): |x-y|>2
nodes.statement_short: Split at |z-y|=|x-y|/2 and use the product inequality for |·|^β∧1.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} \int_{\mathds R^d} \rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz &\leqslant \int_{\{|z-y|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}} \rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz\\ &\quad+\int_{\{|z-y|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}} \rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &=:J_1+J_2. \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (3.3)
nodes.label: l3-2-1a

nodes.statement: \begin{split} \rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)&\preceq \frac{1}{|z-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y). \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (3.4)
nodes.label: l3-2-2

nodes.statement: \begin{split} \big(|x-z|^{\beta_1}\wedge 1\big) \big(|z-y|^{\beta_2}\wedge 1\big)\leqslant &\big(|x-z|^{\beta_1+\beta_2}\wedge 1\big) +\big(|x-z|^{\beta_1}\wedge 1\big) \big(|x-y|^{\beta_2}\wedge 1\big). \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (3.5)
nodes.label: l3-2-3

nodes.statement: \begin{split} J_1&\preceq (t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,\beta_1+\beta_2}_0(t-s,x-z)\,dz\\ &\quad +(t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y)\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,\beta_1}_0(t-s,x-z)\,dz\\ &\preceq (t-s)^{\theta_1+[(({\beta_1+\beta_2})/{\alpha(x) })\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2}\big(1\!+\!|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha(x)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\quad+ (t-s)^{[\theta_1+({\beta_1}/{\alpha(x)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2}\big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1=\alpha(x)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y). \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (3.6)
nodes.label: l3-2-4

nodes.statement: \begin{split} \big(|x-z|^{\beta_1}\wedge 1\big) \big(|z-y|^{\beta_2}\wedge 1\big)\leqslant &\big(|z-y|^{\beta_1+\beta_2}\wedge 1\big) +\big(|z-y|^{\beta_2}\wedge 1\big) \big(|x-y|^{\beta_1}\wedge 1\big), \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (3.7)
nodes.label: l3-2-5

nodes.statement: \begin{split} J_2&\preceq (t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,\beta_1+\beta_2}_0(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\quad +(t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y)\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,\beta_2}_0(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\preceq (t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2+[(({\beta_1+\beta_2})/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1]-1} \big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\quad+ (t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2+[({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1]-1}\big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y), \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (3.8)
nodes.label: l3-2-5a

nodes.statement:
{\bf Case (b): $2t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}\leqslant |x-y|\leqslant 2$.}

Let $J_1$ and $J_2$ be defined by \eqref{l3-2-1a}. If $|z-y|\geqslant
{|x-y|}/{2}$ and $0<s<t<1$, then $|z-y|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$,
and so
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)&\preceq
\begin{cases}
|z-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},& |z-y|\leqslant 1,\\
 |z-y|^{-d-\alpha_1},& |z-y|>1
\end{cases}
\\
&\preceq \begin{cases}
|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},&|z-y|\leqslant 1,\\
|x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1},& |z-y|>1
\end{cases}
\\
&\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in
the third inequality we have used the fact that
$$|x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\quad \textrm{ for all }|x-y|\leqslant 2 ,$$ and the last
inequality follows from
$$|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)} \preceq  \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\quad\textrm{ for all } |x-y|\geqslant 2t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}\geqslant 2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}.$$
Using \eqref{l3-2-6} and following the same argument of \eqref{l3-2-4}, we know that \eqref{l3-2-4} is satisfied too.


If $|z-y|<{|x-y|}/{2}$, then $|x-z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$,
and so we obtain
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)&\preceq
\begin{cases}
|x-z|^{-d-\alpha(z)},& |x-z|\leqslant 1,\\
|x-z|^{-d-\alpha_1}, & |x-z|>1
\end{cases}
\\
&\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(z)} \preceq |x-y|^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)}\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\
&\preceq |x-y|^{-|\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)|}\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\
&\preceq |x-y|^{-C|x-y|^{\beta_0}}\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\
&\preceq \exp\big(C|\log|x-y||\cdot|x-y|^{\beta_0}\big)\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\
&\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where in the second inequality we used the fact that if $|x-z|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$ and $|x-y|\leqslant 2$, then
$|x-z|^{-d-\alpha_1}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(z)},$
the fifth inequality follows from the fact that
$$|\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)|\preceq |z-y|^{\beta_0}\leqslant C |x-y|^{\beta_0}\quad\textrm{ for all }|z-y|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2},$$
in the seventh inequality we used $$\sup_{z\in \mathds R^d: |z|\leqslant 2}\exp\big(C|\log
|z||\cdot|z|^{\beta_0}\big)<\infty,$$ and the last inequality is due to
the same argument of the last one in \eqref{l3-2-6}.


Using the above inequality for $\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)$ and following the same procedure of \eqref{l3-2-5a},
we know that \eqref{l3-2-5a} still holds.

Therefore, according to the estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, \eqref{l3-2-1} also holds in this case.
nodes.name: Case (b): intermediate |x-y|
nodes.statement_short: Same splitting, comparing indices α(z), α(y) via Hölder continuity.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} \rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)&\preceq \begin{cases} |z-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},& |z-y|\leqslant 1,\\ |z-y|^{-d-\alpha_1},& |z-y|>1 \end{cases} \\ &\preceq \begin{cases} |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},&|z-y|\leqslant 1,\\ |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1},& |z-y|>1 \end{cases} \\ &\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y), \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (3.9)
nodes.label: l3-2-6

nodes.statement: \begin{split} \rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)&\preceq \begin{cases} |x-z|^{-d-\alpha(z)},& |x-z|\leqslant 1,\\ |x-z|^{-d-\alpha_1}, & |x-z|>1 \end{cases} \\ &\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(z)} \preceq |x-y|^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)}\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\ &\preceq |x-y|^{-|\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)|}\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\ &\preceq |x-y|^{-C|x-y|^{\beta_0}}\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\ &\preceq \exp\big(C|\log|x-y||\cdot|x-y|^{\beta_0}\big)\cdot|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\\ &\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y), \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (3.10)
nodes.label: l3-2-7

nodes.statement:
{\bf Case (c): $|x-y|\leqslant
2t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}$.}


Note that for any $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
1\leqslant&
\frac{t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}}{t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}}\leqslant
t^{-\frac{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})-\alpha(y)}{\alpha(y)\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}
\leqslant
t^{-\frac{Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant \exp\big(C|\log
t|\cdot t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}} \big)\leqslant C_1 ,
\end{split}
\end{equation}
hence $|x-y|\leqslant 2t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}$
implies that $|x-y|\leqslant C_2 t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$ for some constant
$C_2>0$.

On the other hand,
\begin{align*}
 \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz
&\leqslant \int_{\{|z-y|> t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}\rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz\\
&\quad+\int_{\{|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}\}}\rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{align*}

If $|z-y|\geqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}>s^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, then
\begin{align*}
\rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)\preceq |z-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq t^{-({d+\alpha(y)})/{\alpha(y)}}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where the second inequality follows from $|z-y|\geqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, and the last inequality
is due to $t^{-({d+\alpha(y)})/{\alpha(y)}}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)$ for all $|x-y|\leqslant C_2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$. Applying the above estimate for $\rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)$ and following the same argument of \eqref{l3-2-4}, we can find that \eqref{l3-2-4} still holds
for $J_1$ here.



Now we turn to estimate for $J_2$, which is divided into the following two subcases:

{\bf Subcase (c1): $s>{t}/{2}$.}

If $|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$, then
\begin{align*}
\rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)&\preceq s^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where the second inequality follows
from $s>{t}/{2}$, and in the last inequality we have used the fact that
$t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)$ for all $|x-y|\leqslant C_2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$.

Having the above estimate for $\rho_0^{y,0}(s,z-y)$ at hand, we also can follow the same procedure of \eqref{l3-2-4} to get that \begin{align*}
J_2&\preceq (t-s)^{\theta_1+(({\beta_1+\beta_2})/{\alpha(x)})-1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)+
(t-s)^{\theta_1+({\beta_1}/{\alpha(x)})-1}s^{\theta_2}\rho_0^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y).
\end{align*}


{\bf Subcase (c2): $s\leqslant {t}/{2}$.}

If $|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$,
then we have
\begin{align*}
\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)&\preceq (t-s)^{-({d}/{\alpha(z)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d}/{\alpha(z)})-1}\preceq t^{-|({d}/{\alpha(z)})-({d/\alpha(y)})|}\cdot t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\\
&\preceq t^{-Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}\cdot t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where the second inequality is due to $(t-s)\geqslant {t}/{2}$, in the
fourth inequality we used the fact that
$|\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)|\preceq |z-y|^{\beta_0}\preceq t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha(y)}}\preceq
t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}},$ the fifth inequality follows from
$$\sup_{t \in (0,1]}t^{-Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}\preceq \sup_{t \in (0,1]}
\exp\big(C|\log t|t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}\big)<\infty,$$ and the last
inequality is again due to the fact that $t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq
\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)$ for all $|x-y|\leqslant C_2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$.

Using the above estimate for $\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)$ and following the same procedure of \eqref{l3-2-5a},  we
can also get \eqref{l3-2-5a}.

Combining both estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we know \eqref{l3-2-1} holds for {\bf Case (c)}.
Therefore, the proof of \eqref{l3-2-0} is complete.
nodes.name: Case (c): near diagonal
nodes.statement_short: Split at |z-y|=t^{1/α(y)} and treat s>t/2 and s≤t/2 separately.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} 1\leqslant& \frac{t^{{1}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}}{t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}}\leqslant t^{-\frac{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})-\alpha(y)}{\alpha(y)\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}} \leqslant t^{-\frac{Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant \exp\big(C|\log t|\cdot t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}} \big)\leqslant C_1 , \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (3.11)
nodes.label: l3-2-8

nodes.name: Subcase (c1): s>t/2
nodes.statement_short: Bound ρ_0^{y,0}(s,z-y) by ρ_0^{y,0}(t,x-y).

nodes.statement:
{\bf Subcase (c2): $s\leqslant {t}/{2}$.}

If $|z-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$,
then we have
\begin{align*}
\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)&\preceq (t-s)^{-({d}/{\alpha(z)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d}/{\alpha(z)})-1}\preceq t^{-|({d}/{\alpha(z)})-({d/\alpha(y)})|}\cdot t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\\
&\preceq t^{-Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}\cdot t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq \rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y),
\end{align*}
where the second inequality is due to $(t-s)\geqslant {t}/{2}$, in the
fourth inequality we used the fact that
$|\alpha(y)-\alpha(z)|\preceq |z-y|^{\beta_0}\preceq t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha(y)}}\preceq
t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}},$ the fifth inequality follows from
$$\sup_{t \in (0,1]}t^{-Ct^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}}\preceq \sup_{t \in (0,1]}
\exp\big(C|\log t|t^{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}\big)<\infty,$$ and the last
inequality is again due to the fact that $t^{-({d/\alpha(y)})-1}\preceq
\rho_0^{y,0}(t,x-y)$ for all $|x-y|\leqslant C_2t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}$.

Using the above estimate for $\rho_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z)$ and following the same procedure of \eqref{l3-2-5a},  we
can also get \eqref{l3-2-5a}.

Combining both estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we know \eqref{l3-2-1} holds for {\bf Case (c)}.
Therefore, the proof of \eqref{l3-2-0} is complete.
nodes.name: Subcase (c2): s≤t/2
nodes.statement_short: Bound ρ_0^{z,0}(t-s,x-z) by ρ_0^{y,0}(t,x-y).

nodes.statement:
(2) We can apply the second inequality in \eqref{l3-1-1} in the proofs of
\eqref{l3-2-4} and \eqref{l3-2-5a}, and follow the same arguments as above to prove \eqref{l3-2-1}.
nodes.name: (2) Uniform-index version
nodes.statement_short: Use the second inequality of Lemma 2.1 instead.

nodes.statement: Let $\mathscr{B}(\gamma,\beta)$ denote the Beta function with respect to $\gamma$ and $\beta$. Then, the following two statements hold. \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] For any $\theta_1,\theta_2\in \mathds R$ and $\beta_1,\beta_2 \in (0,1)$, there is a constant $c>0$ such that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $\beta_1+\beta_2<\alpha_*(x,y):=\alpha(x)\wedge\alpha(y)$, $\theta_1+({\beta_1}/{\alpha(x)})>0$ and $\theta_2+({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})>0$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \int_0^t&\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\ \leqslant &c\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_1}/{\alpha_2})+\theta_1,({\beta_2}/{\alpha_2})+\theta_2\big)\\ &\times \Big( \rho_{\theta_1+\theta_2+(({\beta_1+\beta_2})/{\alpha^*(x,y)})}^{y,0}+ \rho_{\theta_1+\theta_2+({\beta_1}/{\alpha(x)})}^{y,\beta_2} +\rho_{\theta_1+\theta_2+({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})}^{y,\beta_1}\Big)(t,x-y), \end{split} \end{equation} where $\alpha^*(x,y):= \alpha(x)\vee\alpha(y)$. \item[(2)] For any $\theta_1,\theta_2\in \mathds R$ and $\beta_1,\beta_2 \in (0,1)$ such that $\beta_1+\beta_2<\alpha_2$, $\theta_1+({\beta_1}/{\alpha_2})>0$ and $\theta_2+({\beta_2}/{\alpha_2})>0$, it holds for any $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ that \begin{equation} \begin{split} \int_0^t&\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho_{\theta_1}^{z,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\ \preceq&\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_1}/{\alpha_2})+\theta_1,({\beta_2}/{\alpha_2})+\theta_2\big) \\ &\times \big( \rho_{\theta_1+\theta_2+(({\beta_1+\beta_2})/{\alpha_2})}^{y,0}+\rho_{\theta_1+\theta_2+({\beta_1}/{\alpha_2})}^{y,\beta_2} +\rho_{\theta_1+\theta_2+({\beta_2}/{\alpha_2})}^{y,\beta_1}\big)(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.name: Corollary 3.2 (time-space convolution inequality)
nodes.statement_short: Integrating Lemma 3.1 in s gives a Beta-function bound for the time-space convolution of two ρ functions.
nodes.label: l3-3

nodes.statement: (1) According to the proofs of \cite[Lemma 2.1 (ii) and (iii)]{CZ}, we know that for $0\leqslant s\leqslant t\leqslant 1$, $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ and $\beta_1,\beta_2 \in (0,1)$, $\theta_1,\theta_2\in \mathds R$, it holds that \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho_{\theta_1}^{y,\beta_1}(t-s,x-z)\rho_{\theta_2}^{y,\beta_2}(s,z-y)\, dz\\ &\preceq \Big[(t-s)^{\theta_1+[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2} \big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\\ &\qquad+(t-s)^{\theta_1} s^{\theta_2 +[((\beta_1+\beta_2)/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1]-1} \big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1+\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\Big]\rho_{0}^{y,0}(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad +(t-s)^{\theta_1+[({\beta_1}/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1]-1}s^{\theta_2} \big(1+|\log (t-s)|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_1=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\rho_{0}^{y,\beta_2}(t,x-y)\\ &\qquad +(t-s)^{\theta_1}s^{\theta_2+[({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})\wedge 1] -1} \big(1+|\log s|\mathds 1_{\{\beta_2=\alpha(y)\}}\big)\rho_0^{y,\beta_1}(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation} If, in addition, $\beta_1+\beta_2<\alpha(x)$, $({\beta_1}/{\alpha(y)})+\theta_1>0$ and $({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})+\theta_2>0$, then it also holds \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,\beta_1}_{\theta_1}(t-s,x-z) \rho^{y,\beta_2}_{\theta_2}(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\ &\preceq \mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_1}/{\alpha(y)})+\theta_1,({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})+\theta_2\big)\\ &\quad \times \big(\rho^{y,0}_{\theta_1+\theta_2+(({\beta_1+\beta_2})/{\alpha(y)})} +\rho^{y,\beta_1}_{\theta_1+\theta_2+({\beta_2}/{\alpha(y)})}(t,x-y) +\rho^{y,\beta_2}_{\theta_1+\theta_2+({\beta_1}/{\alpha(y)})}\big)(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation} Note that in \eqref{l3-2-1-} and \eqref{r3-2-1} the index $\alpha(y)$ is independent of the integrand variable $z$. However, in the present setting we also need \eqref{l3-2-0} and \eqref{l3-2-1} as well as the convolution inequalities \eqref{l3-3-0} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, where the index $\alpha(z)$ will depend on the integrand variable $z$. (2) For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ small enough, $\gamma\in \mathds R$, $\theta \in \mathds R_+$ and $x, y \in \mathds R^d$, define \begin{equation} \tilde \rho_{\gamma,\varepsilon}^{y,\theta }(t,x)=t^{\gamma}(|x|^{\theta}\wedge 1) \begin{cases} \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|x|)^{d+\alpha(y)}},& |x|\leqslant 1,\\ \frac{1}{|x|^{d+\alpha_1-\varepsilon}},& |x|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation} By carefully tracking the proofs of Lemma \ref{l3-1}, Lemma \ref{l3-2}, Corollary \ref{l3-3} and \cite[Lemma 2.1 (ii) and (iii)]{CZ}, we know that the inequalities \eqref{l3-1-1}, \eqref{l3-1-1-00}, \eqref{l3-2-0}, \eqref{l3-2-1}, \eqref{l3-3-0}, \eqref{l3-3-1}, \eqref{l3-2-1-} and \eqref{r3-2-1} are valid with $\rho$ replaced by $\tilde \rho$. (In particular, \eqref{l3-2-6} holds true.) For simplicity, in the remainder of this paper we often omit the parameter $\varepsilon$ in $\tilde \rho$.

nodes.statement: Let $\beta_0^*\in(0,\beta_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2})$ and $\beta_0^{**} \in (0,\beta_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2})$. Then, the following two statements hold. \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then $q(t,x,y):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$ is absolutely convergent on $(0,1]\times \mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d$, it solves equation \eqref{eq2-2} and satisfies that for any $0<\gamma<\theta<{\beta^*_0}/{\alpha_2}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,\theta,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $(t,x,x',y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\leqslant c_1\left(\rho^{y,0}_{{(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)}-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0^*}_{-\gamma}\right)(t,x-y) \end{equation} and if, moreover, $\beta_0^*<\alpha(x)$, then \begin{equation} \begin{split} |q(t,x,y)-q(t,x',y)|\leqslant & c_1\left(|x-x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta^*_0-\alpha_2\theta)}/{\alpha(x)}}\wedge 1\right)\\ &\times\Big[\Big(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0^{*}/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0^*/\alpha_1)} (t,x-y)+\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+ (\beta_0^{*}/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0^*/\alpha_1)}(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{split} \end{equation} Suppose, in addition, that there are $y_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for any $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then there is a constant $c_3:=c_3(\alpha,\kappa,r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y_0)|\leqslant c_3\left(\rho^{y_0,0}_{{\beta_0^*/\alpha_2}}+\rho^{y_0,\beta_0^*}_{0}\right)(t,x-y_0). \end{equation} \item[(2)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<{\beta^{**}_0}/{\alpha_2}$ holds true, then $q(t,x,y)=:\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$ is still absolutely convergent, solves the equation \eqref{eq2-2}, and satisfies that for every $\gamma,\theta>0$ such that $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1+\gamma =:\gamma_2<\theta<{\beta_0^{**}/\alpha_2}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_2:=c_2(\alpha,\kappa, \gamma,\theta,\varepsilon)$ such that for every $(t,x,x',y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\leqslant c_2\left(\rho^{y,0}_{{(\beta_0^{**}/\alpha_2)}-\gamma_2 }+\rho^{y,\beta_0^{**}}_{-\gamma_2 }\right)(t,x-y) \end{equation} and if, moreover, $\beta_0^*<\alpha(x)$, then \begin{equation} \begin{split} |q(t,x,y)-q(t,x',y)| &\leqslant c_2\left(|x-x'|^{{\alpha_1(\beta_0^*-\alpha_2\theta)}/{\alpha(x)}}\wedge 1\right)\\ &\quad\times \Big[\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma_2+(\beta_0^{*}/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0^*/\alpha_1)}(t,x-y) +\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma_2 +(\beta_0^{*}/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0^*/\alpha_1)}(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{split} \end{equation} If additionally there are some $y_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$, then there is a constant $c_4:=c_4(\alpha,\kappa, r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y_0)|\leqslant c_4\left(\rho^{y_0,0}_{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})+{(\beta_0^{**}/\alpha_2)}}+\rho^{y_0,\beta_0^{**}}_{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}\right)(t,x-y_0). \end{equation} \end{itemize}

nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, throughout the proof we will assume that $\beta_0< \alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$; otherwise, we will replace $\beta_0$ by $\beta_0^*.$ (i) According to \eqref{l2-1-2}, if $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then $$|q_0(t,x,y)|\preceq \rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y),\quad t\in(0,1] \textrm{ and } x,y \in \mathds R^d.$$ Therefore, by Corollary \ref{l3-3}, \begin{align*}|q_1(t,x,y)|\preceq&\int_0^t\int \rho_{-\gamma}^{z,\beta_0}(t-s,x-z) \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\ \preceq& \mathscr{B}\big(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, ({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big) \big(\rho_{2(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0}\big)(t,x-y),\end{align*} where $\widehat \beta_0:=\beta_0 \wedge (\alpha_2/2)$. Suppose now that $$|q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant \omega_n\Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),\quad n\geqslant0,$$ where the constant $\omega_n$ is to be determined later. Hence, according to Corollary \ref{l3-3} again, \begin{align*}|q_{n+1}(t,x,y)|\leqslant& C\int_0^t\int \rho_{-\gamma}^{z,\beta_0}(t-s,x-z) \omega_n \Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\ \leqslant&C \omega_n \mathscr{B}(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)) \Big(\rho_{(n+2)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y)\\ =&: \omega_{n+1}\Big(\rho_{(n+2)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y), \end{align*} where $$ \omega_{n+1}= C \mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\omega_n ,$$ and $C$ is a constant independent of $t,n,x$ and $y$. Note that $\omega_0\leqslant C$ and $\mathscr{B}(\gamma, \beta)=\frac{\Gamma(\gamma)\Gamma(\beta)}{\Gamma(\gamma+\beta)}$, where $\Gamma$ is the standard Gamma function. By iteration procedure we have \begin{align*}\omega_n\leqslant &C^{n+1}\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, n(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\\ &\times\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n-1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\cdots\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, ({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big)\\ =&\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}.\end{align*} Therefore, \begin{equation}\begin{split} |q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant &\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)} \Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0} +\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),\end{split} \end{equation} and so combing all estimates together $$\sum_{n=0}^\infty |q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant \left(\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}\right)\Big(\rho_{2(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),$$ which means that $q(t,x,y):=\sum_{n=0}^\infty q_n(t,x,y)$ is absolutely convergent, and $$|q(t,x,y)|\leqslant C_1 \Big(\rho_{2(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y).$$ Thus, \eqref{p3-1-1} is proved by using the fact that $\beta_0\leqslant 2\widehat \beta_0$ and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly. From \eqref{eq3-1} and the fact $q(t,x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$, it is easy to see that $q(t,x,y)$ solves the equation \eqref{eq2-2}. (ii) Suppose that there are some $y_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z\in B(y_0,r_0)$. According to \eqref{l2-1-33a}, it is easy to verify that for every $z \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} |q_0(s,z,y_0)|&\preceq \big(|z-y_0|^{\beta_0}\wedge 1\big)\cdot \begin{cases} \frac{1}{(s^{{1/\alpha(y_0)}}+|z-y_0|)^{d+\alpha(y_0)}},& |z-y_0|\leqslant r_0,\\ \frac{1}{|z-y_0|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|z-y_0|> r_0 \end{cases}\\ &\preceq \rho^{y_0,\beta_0}_0(s,z-y_0). \end{split} \end{equation} This along with the fact that $|q_0(t-s,x,z)|\preceq \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(t-s,x-z)$ for every $x,z\in \mathds R^d$ yields that for all $x\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{align*} |q_1(t,x,y_0)|&\preceq \int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(t-s,x-z)\rho^{y_0,\beta_0}_0(s,z-y_0)\,dz\,ds\\ &\leqslant C\mathscr{B}\big(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma,({ \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big) \big(\rho^{y_0,0}_{({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})+(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}+\rho^{y_0,\beta_0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\big)(t,x-y_0). \end{align*} Following the same arguments in part (i), we find that for every $n \geqslant 0$, \begin{align*} |q_n(t,x,y_0)| &\leqslant \frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)} \Big(\rho_{({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})+n(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y_0,0}+\rho_{n(({ \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y_0,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y_0),\end{align*} which implies $q(t,x,y):=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$ is absolutely convergent and gives us \eqref{p3-1-2b} immediately. (iii) It suffices to prove \eqref{p3-1-1a} for the case that $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$ holds with some $R_1>0$, since the case that $|x-x'|>1$ follows from \eqref{p3-1-1} immediately. For any (fixed) $\varepsilon>0$ small enough, let $\tilde \rho^{y,\beta}_{\gamma}$ be defined by \eqref{p3-1-7}. By \eqref{p3-1-1a-1}, we have \begin{equation} \begin{split} &|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\ &\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\times \bigg[\left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\right)(t,x-y) + \left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\bigg], \end{split} \end{equation} where $\tilde \theta:=\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}$. Since $\beta_0^*=\beta_0<\alpha(x)$, by \eqref{e1-3} we can find a constant $R_1>0$ small enough such that $\beta_0< \alpha(x)\wedge\alpha(x')$ for any $x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$. Then, according to \eqref{eq2-2}, it holds that \begin{align*} &|q(t,x,y)-q(t,x',y)|\\ &\leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d} |q_0(t-s,x,z)-q_0(t-s,x',z)||q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\ &\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\\ &\quad\times\bigg\{ \Big[\big(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\big)(t,x-y) + \left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\Big]\\ &\quad \quad+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \Big[\big(\tilde \rho^{z,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\big)(t-s,x-z)\\ &\qquad\qquad\quad\qquad+ \big(\tilde \rho^{z,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})} \big)(t-s,x'-z)\Big] \Big[\big( \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\big)(s,z-y)\Big]\,dz\,ds \bigg\}\\ &\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\cdot\Big[\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-2\gamma +(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x-y) + \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-2\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{align*} Here the second inequality follows from \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{p3-1-8a}, thanks to the fact that $\beta_0< \alpha(x)\wedge \alpha(x')$, and the last inequality is due to Remark \ref{r3-3}(2) (which indicates that the convolution inequality \eqref{l3-3-0} holds for $\tilde \rho$) and the fact that $\gamma<\theta$. (iv) Now we are going to prove the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$. Due to the assumption $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<{\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$, we can choose $\gamma>0$ small enough such that $\gamma+({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1=:\gamma_2 <{\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$. Using \eqref{l2-1-1} and following the same arguments in part (i) with $\gamma_2 $ instead of $\gamma$, we can obtain that for every $n\geqslant 1$ and $(t,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} |q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant &\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 )\big)} \bigg(\rho_{(n+1)(({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma_2 )}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma_2 +n({\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2} -\gamma_2 )}^{y,\beta_0} \bigg)(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation} Using this and \eqref{l2-1-1}, we find immediately that $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}|q_n(t,x,y)|<\infty$ and so \eqref{p3-1-2} is true. Note that, according to Proposition \ref{p3-1-1a-p}(2), in this case \eqref{p3-1-8a} holds with $\gamma_2$ in place of $\gamma $. (Note that here $\beta_0$ is not replaced by $\beta_0^{**}$.) This along with \eqref{p3-1-2} and the same argument in (iii) gives us \eqref{p3-1-2a}. (v) Suppose that the assumptions in part (2) of the Proposition hold, and that there are some $y_0\in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(y_0)$ for all $z \in B(y_0,r_0)$. Then, using \eqref{l2-1-33} and repeating the arguments in part (ii) above, we can prove \eqref{p3-1-2c}.

nodes.statement_short: Bound q_n inductively via Corollary 3.2 with Gamma-function constants, sum the series; Hölder estimate from the integral equation and Proposition 2.9. Key step: ω_n ≤ [CΓ(·)]^{n+1}/Γ((n+1)(·)).

nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, throughout the proof we will assume that $\beta_0< \alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$; otherwise, we will replace $\beta_0$ by $\beta_0^*.$

nodes.section: 3.2 Existence, upper bounds and continuity of $q(t,x,y)$.

nodes.statement:
(i) According to \eqref{l2-1-2}, if $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then
$$|q_0(t,x,y)|\preceq \rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0}(t,x-y),\quad t\in(0,1] \textrm{ and } x,y \in \mathds R^d.$$
Therefore, by Corollary \ref{l3-3},
\begin{align*}|q_1(t,x,y)|\preceq&\int_0^t\int \rho_{-\gamma}^{z,\beta_0}(t-s,x-z) \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\
\preceq& \mathscr{B}\big(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, ({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big)
\big(\rho_{2(({\widehat
\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0}\big)(t,x-y),\end{align*}
where $\widehat \beta_0:=\beta_0 \wedge (\alpha_2/2)$.


Suppose now that
$$|q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant \omega_n\Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),\quad n\geqslant0,$$
where the constant $\omega_n$ is to be determined later.
Hence, according to Corollary \ref{l3-3} again,
\begin{align*}|q_{n+1}(t,x,y)|\leqslant& C\int_0^t\int \rho_{-\gamma}^{z,\beta_0}(t-s,x-z) \omega_n \Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\
\leqslant&C \omega_n \mathscr{B}(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)) \Big(\rho_{(n+2)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y)\\
=&: \omega_{n+1}\Big(\rho_{(n+2)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma+(n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y), \end{align*} where $$ \omega_{n+1}= C \mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\omega_n ,$$
and $C$ is a constant independent of $t,n,x$ and $y$.
Note that $\omega_0\leqslant C$ and $\mathscr{B}(\gamma, \beta)=\frac{\Gamma(\gamma)\Gamma(\beta)}{\Gamma(\gamma+\beta)}$, where $\Gamma$ is the standard Gamma function. By iteration procedure we have
\begin{align*}\omega_n\leqslant &C^{n+1}\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, n(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\\
&\times\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, (n-1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)\cdots\mathscr{B}\big(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma, ({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma\big)\\
=&\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}.\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant &\frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)} \Big(\rho_{(n+1)(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}
+\rho_{-\gamma+n(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),\end{split}
\end{equation}
and so combing all estimates together
$$\sum_{n=0}^\infty |q_n(t,x,y)|\leqslant \left(\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma )\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)}\right)\Big(\rho_{2(({\widehat \beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y),$$ which means that $q(t,x,y):=\sum_{n=0}^\infty q_n(t,x,y)$ is absolutely convergent, and
$$|q(t,x,y)|\leqslant C_1  \Big(\rho_{2(({\widehat\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{-\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y).$$
Thus, \eqref{p3-1-1} is proved by using the fact that $\beta_0\leqslant 2\widehat \beta_0$ and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly. From \eqref{eq3-1}
and the fact $q(t,x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$, it is easy to see that $q(t,x,y)$ solves the equation \eqref{eq2-2}.

nodes.statement:
(iii) It suffices to prove \eqref{p3-1-1a} for the case that $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$  holds with some $R_1>0$, since the case
that $|x-x'|>1$ follows from \eqref{p3-1-1} immediately.
For any (fixed) $\varepsilon>0$ small enough, let $\tilde \rho^{y,\beta}_{\gamma}$ be defined by \eqref{p3-1-7}.  By \eqref{p3-1-1a-1}, we have
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\times \bigg[\left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\right)(t,x-y)  + \left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\bigg],
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where $\tilde \theta:=\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha(x)}$. Since $\beta_0^*=\beta_0<\alpha(x)$, by  \eqref{e1-3} we can find a constant
$R_1>0$ small enough such that $\beta_0< \alpha(x)\wedge\alpha(x')$ for any $x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$.
Then, according to \eqref{eq2-2}, it holds that
\begin{align*}
&|q(t,x,y)-q(t,x',y)|\\
&\leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
|q_0(t-s,x,z)-q_0(t-s,x',z)||q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\\
&\quad\times\bigg\{ \Big[\big(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\big)(t,x-y)
+ \left(\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}\right)(t,x'-y)\Big]\\
&\quad \quad+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \Big[\big(\tilde \rho^{z,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x)})}\big)(t-s,x-z)\\
&\qquad\qquad\quad\qquad+ \big(\tilde \rho^{z,0}_{\theta-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha(x')})}
\big)(t-s,x'-z)\Big]
\Big[\big(
\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\big)(s,z-y)\Big]\,dz\,ds \bigg\}\\
&\preceq (|x-x'|^{\tilde \theta}\wedge 1)\cdot\Big[\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-2\gamma
+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x-y)
+ \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-2\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x'-y)\Big].
\end{align*}
Here the second inequality follows from \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{p3-1-8a}, thanks to the fact that
$\beta_0< \alpha(x)\wedge \alpha(x')$, and the last inequality is due to Remark \ref{r3-3}(2) (which indicates that the convolution inequality \eqref{l3-3-0} holds for $\tilde \rho$) and the fact that $\gamma<\theta$.

nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Then there exists a constant $c_5:=c_5(\alpha,\kappa)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\leqslant \begin{cases} c_5t^{-1-({d}/{\alpha(y)})},\quad& |x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}},\\ \frac{c_5}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}},\quad& t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}< |x-y| \leqslant 1,\\ \frac{c_5}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\quad& |x-y|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation} \item[(2)] Let $\beta_0^{**}\in(0,\beta_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$, and $\beta_0^{**}/{\alpha_2}>({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$. Then exists a constant $c_6:=c_6(\alpha,\kappa)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\leqslant \begin{cases} c_6t^{-1-({d}/{\alpha(y)})},\quad& |x-y|\leqslant t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}},\\ \frac{c_6t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}},\quad& t^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}< |x-y| \leqslant 1,\\ \frac{c_6t^{1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\quad& |x-y|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation} \end{itemize}

nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, throughout the proof we still assume that $\beta_0< \alpha_2/2$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$. We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. As in the proof of Proposition \ref{p3-1}(1), we know that $q(t,x,y)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q_n(t,x,y)$ is absolutely convergent. In particular, \begin{equation} |q(t,x,y)|\leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)|+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|q_n(t,x,y)|. \end{equation} According to \eqref{p3-1-6a}, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|q_n(t,x,y)| & \leqslant \left(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\big[C \Gamma(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big]^{n+1}}{\Gamma\big((n+1)(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)\big)} \right)\Big(\rho_{3(({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma)}^{y,0}+\rho_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-2\gamma}^{y,\beta_0} \Big)(t,x-y) \preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y), \end{align*} where in the last inequality we choose $\gamma>0$ small enough such that $\gamma<{\beta_0}/({2\alpha_2})$. Combining this estimate with \eqref{p2-1-1} and \eqref{p3-1-9}, we obtain \eqref{p3-1-2e} immediately. If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}>({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$, then one can use \eqref{p2-1-1a} and follow the same procedure above to prove \eqref{p3-1-2f}.

nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by \eqref{eq2-1}, and for every $\gamma,c_0>0$, there exist positive constants $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,c_0)$ and $R_0:=R_0(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,c_0)$ such that for any $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\leqslant \begin{cases} c_1t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}, & |y-x|\leqslant c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x)}},\\ \frac{c_1t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},& c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |y-x|\leqslant R_0,\\ \frac{c_1t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|y-x|> R_0. \end{cases} \end{equation} Suppose additionally that there are some $x_0 \in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for every $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$. Then we can find a constant $c_2:=c_2(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,r_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\leqslant \begin{cases} \frac{c_2 t }{(t^{{1/\alpha(x_0)}}+|x_0-y|)^{d+\alpha(x_0)}},& |x_0-y|\leqslant {r_0}/{2},\\ \frac{c_2 t^{1-\gamma} }{|x_0-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|x_0-y|>{r_0}/{2}. \end{cases} \end{equation} \item[(2)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and $({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1<\min\{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2},1/2\}$, then $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by \eqref{eq2-1}, and for every $\gamma, c_0>0$, there exist constants $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,c_0)$ and $R_0:=R_0(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,c_0)$ such that for any $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\leqslant \begin{cases}c_1t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}, & |y-x|\leqslant c_0 t^{{1/\alpha(x)}},\\ \frac{c_1t^{1-\tilde\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},& c_0 t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |y-x|\leqslant R_0,\\ \frac{c_1t^{1-\tilde\gamma }}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|y-x|> R_0, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $\tilde\gamma:=({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1+\gamma$. Suppose additionally there exist some $x_0 \in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for every $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$. Then, for any $c_0>0$, we can find a constant $c_2:=c_2(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,r_0,c_0)>0$ such that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x_0,y)\leqslant \begin{cases} {c_2}{t^{-{d/\alpha (x_0)}}},&\quad |y-x_0|< c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x_0)}},\\ \frac{c_2 t^{2-{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}} }{|y-x_0|^{d+\alpha(x_0)}},& \quad c_0t^{{1/\alpha(x_0)}}\leqslant |y-x_0|< {r_0}/{2},\\ \frac{c_2 t^{1-\tilde\gamma} }{|x-y_0|^{d+\alpha_1}},&\quad |y-x_0|\geqslant {r_0}/{2}. \end{cases} \end{equation} \end{itemize}
