nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, throughout this proof we will assume that $2\beta_0<\alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$; otherwise, we will replace $\beta_0$ by $\beta_0^{**}\in (0,\beta_0]\cap (0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ For simplicity, we only verify the case that $c_0=1$. (i) We first consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Note that $$p^z(t,x-z)\preceq \rho_1^{z,0}(t,x-z),\quad t\in (0,1],x,z\in \mathds R^d.$$ This, along with \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, yields that for every $(t,x,y)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$ and {any constant $0<\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2},$} \begin{equation*} \int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d} p^z(t-s,x- z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\preceq \big(\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}+ \rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\big)\big(t,x-y\big). \end{equation*} Therefore, $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by \eqref{eq2-1}, and \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\preceq \Big(\rho^{y,0}_1+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}+ \rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\Big)\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq \big(\rho^{y,0}_1+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}\big)\big(t,x-y\big). \end{equation} When $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha_2}}$, $$\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq t^{-\gamma}|x-y|^{\beta_0}\rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big) \preceq t^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big).$$ Hence, due to $\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we get \begin{equation} \begin{split} p(t,x,y)\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(y)}}\preceq t^{-{d}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}, \end{split} \end{equation} where the third inequality follows from \eqref{l3-2-8}. Next, we will verify the other two cases in the upper bound \eqref{p3-2-1}. Observe that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ such that $|x-y|\leqslant 1$ and $|z|\leqslant 1$, \begin{align*} \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}} &= \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{({1/\alpha(y)})-({1/\alpha(x)})}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}} \preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\ &\preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}+|z|t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}})^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\ &=t^{-{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|(d+\alpha(y))}/{\alpha_1^2}}\cdot\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)}}\cdot \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}}\\ &\preceq t^{-{(d+\alpha_2)|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}\cdot t^{-{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1}}\cdot \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}} \preceq \frac{t^{-C_1R_0^{\beta_0}}}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}}, \end{align*} where the second inequality we used $t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant 1$, and the third inequality follows from the fact that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|z|\leqslant 1$, \begin{align*} \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)}}\preceq t^{-{|\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)|}/{\alpha(x)}}. \end{align*} Thus, choosing $R_0:=R_0(\alpha,\gamma)$ small enough such that $C_1R_0^{\beta_0}<\gamma$ and using the definition of $\rho^{x,0}_0$, we can get that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$ and $|z|\leqslant 1$, \begin{equation} \rho^{y,0}_0(t,z)\preceq t^{-\gamma}\rho^{x,0}_0(t,z). \end{equation} By the definition of \eqref{e3-0}, we know immediately that \eqref{l4-1-5} still holds for every $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$ and $|z|> 1$. This is, \eqref{l4-1-5} holds for all $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$. Hence, combining \eqref{p3-2-3}, \eqref{p3-2-3a} with \eqref{l4-1-5} and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly, we find that \begin{align*} p(t,x,y)&\preceq \big(\rho^{y,0}_{1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma} \big)\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq \begin{cases}t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}, & |y-x|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}},\\ \frac{t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},& t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |y-x|\leqslant R_0,\\ \frac{t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|y-x|> R_0. \end{cases} \end{align*} (ii) If there are some $x_0 \in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for all $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$, then for every $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$ and $z \in B(y,{r_0}/{2})$, $ \alpha(z)=\alpha(y)=\alpha(x_0). $ Hence, by \eqref{p3-1-2b}, we have \begin{equation*} |q(t,x,y)|\preceq \Big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_0\Big)(t,x-y)\quad\textrm{ for all } x\in \mathds R^d\textrm{ and }y \in B\big(x_0,{r_0}/{2}\big). \end{equation*} Based on the inequality above, the computation in part (i) is valid with $\gamma=0$ for $x=x_0$ and $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$, which proves \eqref{p3-2-2} for the case that $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$. The upper bound for the case $|y-x_0|>{r_0}/{2}$ is just the same as that of \eqref{p3-2-1}. (iii) If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, then, according to \eqref{p3-1-2}, we know that the computation in part (i) holds with $\gamma$ replaced by $\tilde\gamma$. Thus, following the argument in part (i), we can obtain \eqref{p3-2-1a}. Similarly as in (ii), \eqref{p3-2-2a} could be verified by using \eqref{p3-1-2c}.
nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.1 (existence and upper bounds of p)
nodes.statement_short: Combine p^z ≤ ρ_1^{z,0} with the bound on q and the convolution inequality, then compare ρ^{y,0} with ρ^{x,0} for nearby x,y.

nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, throughout this proof we will assume that $2\beta_0<\alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$; otherwise, we will replace $\beta_0$ by $\beta_0^{**}\in (0,\beta_0]\cap (0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ For simplicity, we only verify the case that $c_0=1$.
nodes.name: WLOG
nodes.statement_short: Assume 2β_0<α_2 and c_0=1.

nodes.statement:
(i) We first consider the case that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
Note that $$p^z(t,x-z)\preceq \rho_1^{z,0}(t,x-z),\quad t\in (0,1],x,z\in \mathds R^d.$$ This, along with
\eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, yields that for every $(t,x,y)\in
(0,1]\times \mathds R^d \times \mathds R^d$ and {any constant
$0<\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2},$}
\begin{equation*}
\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d} p^z(t-s,x-
z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\preceq
\big(\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}+
\rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\big)\big(t,x-y\big).
\end{equation*}
Therefore, $p(t,x,y)$ is well defined by \eqref{eq2-1}, and
\begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\preceq \Big(\rho^{y,0}_1+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}+
\rho^{y,0}_{1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\Big)\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq
\big(\rho^{y,0}_1+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}\big)\big(t,x-y\big).
\end{equation}

When $|x-y|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha_2}}$,
$$\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq t^{-\gamma}|x-y|^{\beta_0}\rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big)
\preceq t^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big).$$
Hence, due to $\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we get
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
p(t,x,y)\preceq \rho^{y,0}_1\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(y)}}\preceq
t^{-{d}/{\overline{\alpha}(y;t^{{1/\alpha_2}})}}\preceq t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}},
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where the third inequality follows from \eqref{l3-2-8}.

Next, we will verify the other two cases in the upper bound \eqref{p3-2-1}. Observe that
for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ such that
$|x-y|\leqslant 1$ and $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
 \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(y)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}
&=
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{({1/\alpha(y)})-({1/\alpha(x)})}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}
 \preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\
&\preceq \frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}+|z|t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}})^{d+\alpha(y)}}\\
&=t^{-{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|(d+\alpha(y))}/{\alpha_1^2}}\cdot\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)}}\cdot
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}}\\
&\preceq t^{-{(d+\alpha_2)|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}\cdot
t^{-{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1}}\cdot
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}} \preceq
\frac{t^{-C_1R_0^{\beta_0}}}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{d+\alpha(x)}},
\end{align*}
where the second inequality we used
$t^{{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(y)|}/{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant 1$, and the third inequality follows from the fact that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{(t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}+|z|)^{\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)}}\preceq t^{-{|\alpha(y)-\alpha(x)|}/{\alpha(x)}}.
\end{align*}
Thus, choosing $R_0:=R_0(\alpha,\gamma)$ small enough  such that
$C_1R_0^{\beta_0}<\gamma$ and using the definition of $\rho^{x,0}_0$, we can
get that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with
$|x-y|\leqslant R_0$ and $|z|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{equation} \rho^{y,0}_0(t,z)\preceq t^{-\gamma}\rho^{x,0}_0(t,z).
\end{equation}
By the definition of \eqref{e3-0}, we know immediately that \eqref{l4-1-5} still holds for
every $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$ and $|z|> 1$. This is, \eqref{l4-1-5} holds for all $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_0$.

Hence, combining \eqref{p3-2-3}, \eqref{p3-2-3a} with \eqref{l4-1-5} and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly, we find that
\begin{align*}
p(t,x,y)&\preceq
 \big(\rho^{y,0}_{1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{1-\gamma}
\big)\big(t,x-y\big)\preceq \begin{cases}t^{-{d/\alpha(x)}}, & |y-x|\leqslant t^{{1/\alpha(x)}},\\
\frac{t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}},& t^{{1/\alpha(x)}}\leqslant |y-x|\leqslant R_0,\\
\frac{t^{1-\gamma}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},&|y-x|> R_0.
\end{cases}
\end{align*}

nodes.statement:
(ii) If there are some $x_0 \in \mathds R^d$ and $r_0\in(0,\infty]$ such
that $\alpha(z)=\alpha(x_0)$ for all $z \in B(x_0,r_0)$, then for
every $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$ and $z \in
B(y,{r_0}/{2})$,
$
\alpha(z)=\alpha(y)=\alpha(x_0).
$
Hence, by \eqref{p3-1-2b}, we have
\begin{equation*}
|q(t,x,y)|\preceq
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_0\Big)(t,x-y)\quad\textrm{ for all }
x\in \mathds R^d\textrm{ and }y \in B\big(x_0,{r_0}/{2}\big).
\end{equation*}
Based on the inequality above, the computation in part (i) is valid
with $\gamma=0$ for $x=x_0$ and $y \in B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$, which
proves \eqref{p3-2-2} for the case that $y \in
B(x_0,{r_0}/{2})$. The upper bound for the case
$|y-x_0|>{r_0}/{2}$ is just the same as that of \eqref{p3-2-1}.

nodes.statement:
(iii) If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and
${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, then, according to
\eqref{p3-1-2}, we know that the computation in part (i) holds with
$\gamma$ replaced by $\tilde\gamma$. Thus, following the argument in part
(i), we can obtain \eqref{p3-2-1a}. Similarly as in (ii),
\eqref{p3-2-2a} could be verified by using \eqref{p3-1-2c}.

nodes.statement: The estimate \eqref{p3-2-2} indicates that if $\alpha(x)$ is a constant $\alpha\in(0,2)$ locally, then we can get a upper bound for $p(t,x,y)$ which is also locally comparable with that for the heat kernel of rotationally symmetric $\alpha$-stable process. In particular, when $\alpha(x)\equiv\alpha$ for all $x \in \mathds R^d$, \eqref{p3-2-2a} coincides with the upper bound given in \cite[Therem 1.1]{CZ}.
nodes.name: Remark 4.2 (locally constant index)

nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item [(1)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then for any $c_0>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,c_0)$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\leqslant \begin{cases} c_1t^{-{d}/{\alpha(x)}},\quad& |x-y|\leqslant c_0t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}},\\ \frac{c_1t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}},\quad& c_0 t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}< |x-y| \leqslant 1,\\ \frac{c_1t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\quad& |x-y|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation} \item [(2)] Let $\beta_0^{**}\in(0,\beta_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${\beta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}>({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$. Then, for any $c_0>0$, there exists a positive constant $c_2:=c_2(\alpha,\kappa,c_0)$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)\leqslant \begin{cases} c_2t^{-{d}/{\alpha(x)}},\quad& |x-y|\leqslant c_0t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}},\\ \frac{c_2t^{2-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}},\quad& c_0t^{{1}/{\alpha(x)}}< |x-y| \leqslant 1,\\ \frac{c_2t^{2-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\quad& |x-y|>1. \end{cases} \end{equation} \end{itemize}

nodes.statement: Throughout the proof, we assume that $\beta_0<\alpha_2/2$ and that $\beta_0=\beta_0^{**}.$ We only verify the case that $c_0=1$. (1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. {\bf Case (a): $|x-y|\leqslant t^{1/\alpha(x)}$.} According to \eqref{p3-2-1}, we can easily see that \eqref{p3-3-1} holds. {\bf Case (b): $|x-y|>2$.} We have \begin{equation} \begin{split} \left|\int_{\mathds R^d} p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right| &\leqslant \int_{\{|z-y|>{|x-y|}/{2}\}} p^z(t-s,x-z)|q(s,z,y)|\,dz\\ &\quad +\int_{\{|z-y|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\}} p^z(t-s,x-z)|q(s,z,y)|\,dz\\ &=:J_1+J_2. \end{split} \end{equation}When $|z-y|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\geqslant 1$, it follows from \eqref{p3-1-2e} that for any $s\in (0,1]$ and $y,z\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation*} |q(s,z,y)|\preceq \frac{1}{|z-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}. \end{equation*} Therefore, by \eqref{p1-1-1-1-0} and \eqref{l3-1-1}, \begin{align*} J_1&\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)\, dz\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}. \end{align*} Meanwhile, it is not difficult to see that condition $|z-y|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$ implies $|z-x|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}\geqslant 1$, and so \begin{equation*} p^z(t-s,x-z)\preceq \frac{t-s}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq \frac{t}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1}}. \end{equation*} This, along with \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-1-1-00}, yields that \begin{align*} J_2&\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\left( \rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\rho^{y, \beta_0}_{-\gamma}\right)(s,z-y)\, dz\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\cdot s^{-1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}. \end{align*} Combining all the estimates above together and choosing $0<\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we find that \begin{align*} \left|\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\right| &\preceq \int_0^t (J_1+J_2)\,ds\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\cdot \big(1+t^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\big)\!\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}. \end{align*} Then, the desired assertion \eqref{p3-3-1} immediately follows from the estimate above and \eqref{eq2-1}. {\bf Case (c): $t^{{1}/ \alpha(x)}\leqslant |x-y|\leqslant 2$.} We still define $J_1$ and $J_2$ by those in \eqref{p3-3-2}. If $|z-y|\geqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$, then, by \eqref{p3-1-2e}, we have \begin{align*} |q(s,z,y)|&\preceq \begin{cases} s^{-d/\alpha(y)},& |z-y|\leqslant s^{1/\alpha(y)},\\ |z-y|^{-d-\alpha_2},& s^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\leqslant|z-y|\leqslant 1,\\ |z-y|^{-d-\alpha_1},& |z-y|>1 \end{cases} \\ &\preceq \begin{cases} |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},& |z-y|\leqslant s^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}},\\ |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_2},& s^{{1}/{\alpha(y)}}\leqslant|z-y|\leqslant 1,\\ |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1},& |z-y|>1 \end{cases} \\ &\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_2}, \end{align*} where in the second inequality we have used that fact that if $|z-y|\leqslant s^{1/\alpha(y)}$ and $|x-y|\preceq |z-y|$, then $$s^{-d/\alpha(y)}\preceq |z-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},$$ the last inequality follows from the fact that $|x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_2}$, thanks to $|x-y|\leqslant 2$. Hence, \begin{align*} J_1&\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}} \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)\,dz \preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}. \end{align*} At the same time, if $|z-y|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$, then \begin{align*} p^z(t-s,x-z)&\preceq \frac{t-s}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha(z)}}\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(z)}}\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}, \end{align*} where the last inequality follows from $|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(z)}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_2}$ since $|x-y|\leqslant 2$. Combining this estimate with \eqref{p3-1-1}, we arrive at $$ J_2 \preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\left( \rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\right)(s,z-y)\,dz \preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}\cdot s^{-1+(\beta_0/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}. $$ Using all the estimates above and choosing $0<\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we get \begin{align*} \left|\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\right| &\preceq \int_0^t (J_1+J_2)\,ds\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}\cdot \left(1+t^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\right)\!\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}. \end{align*} This, along with \eqref{eq2-1} immediately yields \eqref{p3-3-1}. (2) If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}>({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1$, then, applying \eqref{p3-1-2f} and following the same arguments as above, we can prove \eqref{p3-1-1a}. The details are omitted here.

\\

\end{align*}
where in the second inequality we have used that fact that if
$|z-y|\leqslant s^{1/\alpha(y)}$ and $|x-y|\preceq |z-y|$, then
$$s^{-d/\alpha(y)}\preceq |z-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha(y)},$$
the last inequality follows from the fact that $|x-y|^{-d-\alpha_1}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_2}$, thanks to $|x-y|\leqslant 2$.
Hence,
\begin{align*}
J_1&\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}} \int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)\,dz \preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}.
\end{align*}
At the same time, if $|z-y|\leqslant {|x-y|}/{2}$, then
\begin{align*}
p^z(t-s,x-z)&\preceq \frac{t-s}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha(z)}}\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(z)}}\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}},
\end{align*}
where the last inequality follows from $|x-y|^{-d-\alpha(z)}\preceq |x-y|^{-d-\alpha_2}$ since $|x-y|\leqslant 2$.
Combining this estimate with \eqref{p3-1-1},  we arrive at
$$
J_2 \preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\left(
\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\right)(s,z-y)\,dz \preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}\cdot s^{-1+(\beta_0/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}.
$$

Using all the estimates above and choosing $0<\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we get
\begin{align*}
 \left|\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\right|
&\preceq \int_0^t (J_1+J_2)\,ds\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}\cdot \left(1+t^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\right)\!\preceq \frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_2}}.
\end{align*}
This, along with \eqref{eq2-1} immediately yields \eqref{p3-3-1}.

The third and the fourth equalities above follow from the following facts respectively  egin{align*} \int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^x f(z_1) g(z_1) \,dz_1=\int_{\mathds R^d} f(z_1) {\mathcal L}^x g(z_1) \,dz_1,\quad f,g \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathds R^d), \end{align*}  egin{align*} \int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^y f(z_1) g(z_1)\, dz_1=\int_{\mathds R^d} f(z_1) {\mathcal L}^y g(z_1) \, dz_1, \quad f,g \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathds R^d) \end{align*} and  egin{align*} \int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^x f(z_1)\,dz_1=\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^y f(z_1)\,dz_1=0,\quad f \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathds R^d). \end{align*} Note that, also due to estimates for $p^x(\cdot, \cdot)$ and $p^y(\cdot, \cdot)$, the equalities above are still true for $p^x(t,\cdot)$ and $p^y(t,\cdot)$. p^y(t-s,z-w)\Big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big) p^x(s,w)\,\nabla p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\quad +\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \nabla p^x(s,w)\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)
p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big) p^x(s,w)
\big(\nabla p^y(t-s,z-w)-\nabla p^y(t-s,z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&\quad +\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d} \big(\nabla p^x(s,w)-\nabla p^x(s,z)\big)  \big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)
p^y(t-s,z-w)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&=:I_1+I_2,
\end{align*} where in the first and the second equalities we used the integration by part formula
and  in the second equality we also used the fact that $\nabla  {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,w)= {\mathcal L}^x \nabla p^y(t,w)$.

Observe that
$$
t^{-d/\alpha(y)}\leqslant t^{-d/\alpha(x)}t^{-\big|\frac{d}{\alpha(y)}-\frac{d}{\alpha(x)}\big|}\leqslant
t^{-d/\alpha(x)}t^{-\frac{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)|}{\alpha_1^2}}\leqslant t^{-d/\alpha(x)}t^{-C|x-z|^{\beta_0}}.
$$
Then, according to \eqref{l4-4-1} and the proof of \eqref{l4-1-6},
for any $\theta \in (0,1)$, $\gamma\in (0,1)$, there exists a
constant $R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)\in(0,R_0)$ such that for all $0<t \leqslant 1$ and
 $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\left|\nabla p^y(t,z-w)-\nabla p^y(t,z)\right|\\
&\preceq \big(|w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\big)\cdot
\big[\rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z-w)+\rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Choosing $\theta\in(0,1\wedge \alpha_1)$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\alpha_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\alpha_1}))/2)$, and using
\eqref{l4-1-4} and \eqref{l4-1-7}, we arrive at that for any $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{align*}
I_1&\preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot\bigg(\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,z-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\qquad\qquad \qquad\quad +\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,z)\,dw\,ds\bigg)\\
&=:|x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot \big(I_{11}+I_{12}\big).
\end{align*}
Noticing that, by Remark \ref{r3-3}(2),  \eqref{l3-2-1-} still holds for $\tilde \rho$, we have
\begin{align*}
I_{11}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,z)\int_0^{t/2}
\Big(s^{-\gamma}(t-s)^{-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}+s^{-1+\theta/\alpha_2-\gamma}(t-s)^{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}\Big)\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,z) \cdot t^{1-(1/\alpha(x))-2\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}\preceq
 \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-2\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}(t,z).
\end{align*}
On the other hand, following the argument of  \eqref{l4-1-8}, we can obtain that
\begin{align*}
I_{12}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}(t,z)\cdot\int_0^{t/2}
\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\,dw\,ds\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-2\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}(t,z).
\end{align*}

By the same argument as that for $I_1$, we can also obtain that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and
$x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
I_2\preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x))-2\gamma-(\theta/\alpha_1)}(t,z).
\end{equation*}
Combining all estimates together, we have shown
\eqref{l4-1-1-1}.

Then, for every $\gamma>0$ small enough, there exist positive constants $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$ and $R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,x',y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$ \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big| &\leqslant c_1 |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1} \big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}}(t,x-y)+\rho^{y,0}_{{\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}}(t,x'-y)\big). \end{split} \end{equation} \item[(2)] Let $\beta_0^{**}\in(0,\beta_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}/{2}).$ If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<\beta_0^{**}/{\alpha_2}$, then for every $\gamma>0$, there exist positive constants $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$ and $R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,x',y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_1$ \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big|\leqslant& c_1|x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\gamma_1 }(t,x-y)+ \rho^{y,0}_{\gamma_1 }(t,x'-y)\big), \end{split} \end{equation} where $\gamma_1:=1-({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))$. \end{itemize}

nodes.statement: For simplicity, we assume that $\beta_0< {\alpha_2}/{2}$ and $\beta_0^{**}=\beta_0$ as before. (1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. According to \eqref{p1-1-3}, for any $\gamma>0$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|\\ &\preceq \big[\big((t-s)^{-{1}/{\alpha(z)}}|x-x'|\big)\wedge 1\big]\cdot \big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big]\\ &\preceq \big[\big((t-s)^{-{1}/{\alpha(z)}}|x-x'|\big)^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\wedge 1\big] \big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big]\\ &\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}(t-s)^{-{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+}/{\alpha(z)}} \times\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big]. \end{split} \end{equation} On the one hand, observing that $$\frac{\alpha(x)-\gamma}{\alpha(z)}\leqslant 1+\frac{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)|}{\alpha_1}-\frac{\gamma}{\alpha_2}\leqslant 1+\frac{C|x-z|^{\beta_0}}{\alpha_1}-\frac{\gamma}{\alpha_2},$$ we can find a constant $R_2:=R_2(\alpha,\gamma)>0$ such that for every $x,x',z\in \mathds R^d$ satisfying $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$ and $|x-z|\leqslant 2R_2$ (which imply that $|x'-z|\leqslant 3R_2$), it holds \begin{equation*} \frac{\alpha(x)-\gamma}{\alpha(z)}\leqslant 1-\frac{2\gamma}{3\alpha_2}, \end{equation*} which in turn yields that for every $0<s\leqslant t\leqslant 1$ and $x,x',z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$ and $|x-z|\leqslant 2R_2$ \begin{align*} \big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big| &\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\left(\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t-s,x'-z)\right). \end{align*} On the other hand, when $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$ and $|z-x|>2R_2$ (which imply that $|z-x'|>R_2$), we obtain from \eqref{p1-1-1} and the mean value theorem that \begin{align*} |p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)| &\leqslant |x-x'|\cdot|\nabla p^z(t-s,x-z+\tilde \theta_{x,x',z}(x'-x))|\\ &\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \frac{t-s}{((t-s)^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}+|x-z|)^{d+\alpha(z)+1}}\\ &\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \frac{t-s}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z). \end{align*} where in the first inequality $|\tilde \theta_{x,x'z}|\leqslant 1$ is a constant (which may depend on $x$, $x'$ and $z$), in the second inequality we have used the fact that $$|x-z+\tilde \theta_{x,x',z}(x'-x)|\geqslant |x-z|-|x'-x|\geqslant {|x-z|}/{2},$$ and the fourth inequality follows from $|z-x|>R_2>C(t-s)^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}$. As a result, we obtain that for all $x,x',z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \big|p^z(t,x-z)-p^z(t,x'-z)\big| &\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\Big(\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t,x-z) +\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t,x'-z)\Big). \end{split} \end{equation} Then, using \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1} and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly, we arrive at for every $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$, \begin{align*} &\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)||q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\ &\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\!\cdot\Big[\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})\!+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{{\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}}\Big)(t,x-y)\!+ \Big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})\!+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{{\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}}\Big)(t,x'-y)\Big]. \end{align*} Combining all the estimates together with \eqref{eq2-1} and using again \eqref{pppxy}, we can prove \eqref{t4-2-1} immediately. (2) Now we assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$. Replacing $\alpha(x)$ by $\alpha(z)$ in \eqref{t4-2-1a}, we find that for every $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{align*} &\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|\\ &\preceq (|x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\wedge 1)(t-s)^{-{(\alpha(z)-\gamma)_+}/{\alpha(z)}} \big(\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big)\\ &\preceq (|x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\wedge 1) \big[\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x'-z)\big]. \end{align*} Combining this with \eqref{eq2-1}, \eqref{p3-1-2} and \eqref{l3-3-1}, and following the same arguments above, we arrive at for all $x,x'\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$, \begin{align*} \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big| &\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\\ &\quad\times \Big[\big(\rho^{y,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t,x-y)+ \rho^{y,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t,x'-y)\big)\\ &\qquad\,\,+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \big(\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x'-z)\big)\\ &\qquad \qquad \times \big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-[{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1+{\gamma}/({2\alpha_2})]}+ \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-[{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1+{\gamma}/({2\alpha_2})]}\Big)(s,z-y)\,dz\, ds \Big]\\ &\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1} \big[\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\beta_0/\alpha_2+\gamma_1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\gamma_1}\big)(t,x-y)+ \big(\rho^{y,0}_{\beta_0/\alpha_2+\gamma_1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\gamma_1}\big)(t,x'-y)\big], \end{align*} where $\gamma_1:=1-\alpha_2/\alpha_1+\gamma/(2\alpha_2)$. By now we have verified \eqref{t4-2-1aa}. The proof is complete.

nodes.statement:
(1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. According
to  \eqref{p1-1-3}, for any $\gamma>0$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|\\
&\preceq \big[\big((t-s)^{-{1}/{\alpha(z)}}|x-x'|\big)\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big]\\
&\preceq
\big[\big((t-s)^{-{1}/{\alpha(z)}}|x-x'|\big)^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge
1}\wedge 1\big]
\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big]\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge
1}(t-s)^{-{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+}/{\alpha(z)}}
\times\big[\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x'-z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}

On the one hand, observing that
$$\frac{\alpha(x)-\gamma}{\alpha(z)}\leqslant 1+\frac{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)|}{\alpha_1}-\frac{\gamma}{\alpha_2}\leqslant
1+\frac{C|x-z|^{\beta_0}}{\alpha_1}-\frac{\gamma}{\alpha_2},$$ we can find a constant
$R_2:=R_2(\alpha,\gamma)>0$ such that for every $x,x',z\in \mathds R^d$ satisfying
$|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$ and $|x-z|\leqslant 2R_2$ (which imply that $|x'-z|\leqslant
3R_2$), it holds
\begin{equation*}
\frac{\alpha(x)-\gamma}{\alpha(z)}\leqslant 1-\frac{2\gamma}{3\alpha_2},
\end{equation*}
which in turn yields that for every $0<s\leqslant t\leqslant 1$ and $x,x',z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant
R_2$ and $|x-z|\leqslant 2R_2$
\begin{align*}
\big|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)\big|
&\preceq
|x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\left(\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t-s,x'-z)\right).
\end{align*}

On the other hand, when $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$ and $|z-x|>2R_2$ (which
imply that $|z-x'|>R_2$), we obtain from \eqref{p1-1-1} and the mean
value theorem that
\begin{align*}
|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)|
&\leqslant |x-x'|\cdot|\nabla p^z(t-s,x-z+\tilde \theta_{x,x',z}(x'-x))|\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \frac{t-s}{((t-s)^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}+|x-z|)^{d+\alpha(z)+1}}\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \frac{t-s}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \rho^{z,0}_1(t-s,x-z).
\end{align*}
where in the first inequality $|\tilde \theta_{x,x'z}|\leqslant 1$ is a
constant (which may depend on $x$, $x'$ and $z$), in the second inequality
we have used the fact that
$$|x-z+\tilde \theta_{x,x',z}(x'-x)|\geqslant |x-z|-|x'-x|\geqslant {|x-z|}/{2},$$
and the fourth inequality follows from
$|z-x|>R_2>C(t-s)^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}$.

As a result, we obtain that for all $x,x',z\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
\big|p^z(t,x-z)-p^z(t,x'-z)\big|
&\preceq
|x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\Big(\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t,x-z)
+\rho^{z,0}_{{2\gamma}/({3\alpha_2})}(t,x'-z)\Big).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Then, using \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-3-1} and changing the constant $\gamma$ properly, we arrive at for every
$|x-x'|\leqslant R_2$,
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|p^z(t-s,x-z)-p^z(t-s,x'-z)||q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha(x)-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}\!\cdot\Big[\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})\!+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{{\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}}\Big)(t,x-y)\!+
\Big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})\!+({\gamma}/({2\alpha_2}))}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{{\gamma/(2\alpha_2)}}\Big)(t,x'-y)\Big].
\end{align*}

Combining all the estimates together with \eqref{eq2-1} and using again \eqref{pppxy}, we can prove \eqref{t4-2-1} immediately.

 \big|p(t,x,y)-p(t,x',y)\big|

&\qquad\,\,+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
\big(\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x-z)+\rho^{z,0}_{{\gamma}/{\alpha_2}}(t-s,x'-z)\big)\\
&\qquad \qquad  \times \big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-[{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1+{\gamma}/({2\alpha_2})]}+
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-[{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1+{\gamma}/({2\alpha_2})]}\Big)(s,z-y)\,dz\, ds \Big]\\
&\preceq |x-x'|^{(\alpha_1-\gamma)_+\wedge 1}
\big[\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\beta_0/\alpha_2+\gamma_1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\gamma_1}\big)(t,x-y)+
\big(\rho^{y,0}_{\beta_0/\alpha_2+\gamma_1}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\gamma_1}\big)(t,x'-y)\big],
\end{align*}
where $\gamma_1:=1-\alpha_2/\alpha_1+\gamma/(2\alpha_2)$. By now we have verified \eqref{t4-2-1aa}. The proof is complete.

nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Let $\beta_0^*:=\beta_0\wedge\alpha_2$. If $\tilde \beta_0(x_0):=({\alpha_1\beta_0}/{\alpha(x_0)})\wedge\alpha_1>1-\alpha(x_0)$ for some $x_0 \in \mathds R^d$, then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x=x_0$. Moreover, for every $\gamma>0$, \begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\leqslant c_1\rho^{y,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})+(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)- (\beta_0^*/\alpha_1)-\gamma}(t,x_0-y) \end{equation} holds for some $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,x_0)>0$. \item[(2)] Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<\beta_0^{**}/\alpha_2$, where $\beta_0^{**}:=\beta_0\wedge (\alpha_2/2)$. If $\tilde \beta_0(x_0) -({\alpha_1\alpha_2}/{\alpha(x_0)})(({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1)>1-\alpha_1$ for some $x_0\in \mathds R^d$ with $\tilde \beta_0(x_0)$ defined in $(i)$, then for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x_0\in \mathds R^d$. Furthermore, for every $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant $c_2:=c_2(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,x_0)>0$ such that \begin{equation} |\nabla p(t,\cdot,y)(x_0)|\leqslant c_2\rho^{y,0}_{1-({1}/{\alpha_1})+(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0^*/\alpha_1)-\gamma_2 }(t,x_0-y), \end{equation} where $\gamma_2 :={(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1+\gamma$. \end{itemize}

abla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dzight|\,ds \preceq 	ilde ho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))+( eta_0/\alpha_2)-( eta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y). \end{equation*} According to the estimate above and the dominated convergence theorem, we know that $
abla p(t,\cdot)(x_0)$ exists, and \eqref{t5-1-1} holds by changing $	heta$ and $\gamma$ properly. (2) Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<{ eta_0^{**}}/{\alpha_2}$. If for some $x_0\in \mathds R^d$, $	ilde  eta_0(x_0)-({\alpha_1\alpha_2}/{\alpha(x_0)})  ig(({\alpha_2}/{\alpha_1})-1 ig)>1-\alpha_1$, then, by \eqref{l4-1-1-1} and \eqref{t5-1-3}, $$ |

abla p^x(t,x-z)-

nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the Levi representation under the integral; split the time integral at t/2 and use Hölder continuity of q and Lemma 4.5 to tame the singularity.

nodes.statement:
(1) We first suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. For simplicity, we assume
that $\beta_0< \alpha(x_0)$, and so $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$ and
$\tilde \beta_0(x_0)={\alpha_1\beta_0}/{\alpha(x_0)}$. We will show that we can take the gradient with respect to variable $x$ in the equation \eqref{eq2-1}.
Note that
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^t \left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&=\int_0^{t/2}\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{t/2}^t\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)\left(q(s,z,y)-q(s,x_0,y)\right)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{t/2}^t\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\left(\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)-\nabla p^{x_0}(t-s,x_0-z)\right)
q(s,x_0,y)\,dz\right|\,ds\\
&=:\int_0^{t/2}\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}J_1(s,z)\,dz\right|\,ds+\int_{t/2}^t
\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}J_2(s,z)\,dz\right|\,ds+\int_{t/2}^t
\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}J_3(s,z)\,dz\right|\,ds.
\end{align*}



According to \eqref{p1-1-1},
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|&\preceq \frac{t}{(t^{{1}/{\alpha(z)}}+|x-z|)^{d+\alpha(z)+1}}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Observing that
\begin{equation*}
\Big|\frac{1}{\alpha(z)}-\frac{1}{\alpha(x)}\Big|\leqslant
\frac{|\alpha(x)-\alpha(z)|}{\alpha_1^2}\leqslant C|x-z|^{\beta_0},
\end{equation*}
we find by \eqref{t5-1-3} that for every (small enough) $\gamma>0$, there is a constant $R_1:=R_1(\alpha, \kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
|\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|&\preceq
\begin{cases}
\rho^{z,0}_{1-({1}/{\alpha(z)})}(t,x-z),\ &|x-z|\leqslant R_1,\\
\frac{t}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1+1}}
,\ & |x-z|>R_1
\end{cases}\\
&\preceq \rho^{z,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x)})-\gamma}(t,x-z). \end{split}
\end{equation}

Thus, choosing $\gamma>0$ small enough such that $\gamma<\beta_0/\alpha_2$, and using \eqref{l3-2-0}, \eqref{p3-1-1} and
\eqref{t5-1-4}, we can find that
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^{t/2}\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_1(s,z)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq
\int_0^{t/2}\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)
\big(
\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}(s,z-y)+
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(s,z-y)\big)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x_0-y)\!\bigg(\!\int_0^{t/2}\!(t\!-\!s)^{-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-\gamma}\! +\!
(t\!-\!s)^{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{-1+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-\gamma}\,ds \bigg)\\
&\preceq \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-2\gamma}(t,x-y).
\end{align*}

On the other hand, according to \eqref{p3-1-1a}, \eqref{t5-1-4} and the fact that $\beta_0<\alpha(x_0)$, we arrive at
\begin{align*}
 \int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_2(s,z)|\,dz\,ds
&\preceq \int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
\bigg(\rho^{z,\widehat \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\tilde\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}
(s,z-y)
\\
&\qquad\qquad
+\rho^{z,\widehat \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\tilde\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(s,x_0-y)\bigg)\,dz\,ds\\
&=:\int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}(J_{21}(s,z)+J_{22}(s,z))\,dz\,ds,
\end{align*}
where $\widehat \beta_0=\widehat \beta_0(\theta):={\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)}/{\alpha(x_0)}$.

Since $\tilde \beta_0(x_0)>1-\alpha(x_0)$, we can choose
$\theta, \gamma>0$ small enough such that $1+(\widehat \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma>0$, which along with
\eqref{l3-2-0} yields
\begin{align*}
\int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}J_{21}(s,z)\,dz\,ds
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x_0-y)\cdot\Big(
\int_{t/2}^t (t-s)^{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{-1+\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}\\
&\quad \quad +(t-s)^{(\widehat \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-
(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}\,ds\Big)\\
&\preceq\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y).
\end{align*}
On the other hand, noting that for $t/2<s\leqslant t$, it holds that
\begin{equation} \tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(s,x_0-y)\preceq
\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(t,x_0-y).
\end{equation}
Since $\tilde \beta_0>1-\alpha(x_0)$, by \eqref{l3-1-1} we have
\begin{align*}
 \int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}J_{22}(s,z)\,dz\,ds
&\preceq
\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x_0-y)
\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,\widehat \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1+(\widehat \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-(1/\alpha(x_0))+
(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y).
\end{align*}



According to \eqref{l4-1-1-1} for the case that $|x_0-z|\leqslant R_1$ and \eqref{t5-1-4} for the case
that $|x_0-z|>R_1$), we arrive at that (by changing the constant $\gamma$ properly) for any $t>0$ and $x_0,z\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{align*}
\left|\nabla p^{x_0}(t,x_0-z)-\nabla p^z(t,x_0-z)\right|\preceq
\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{1-1/\alpha(x_0)-\gamma}(t,x_0-z).
\end{align*}
This, along with \eqref{p3-1-1} yields
\begin{align*}
\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_3(s,z)|\,dz\,ds
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{-\gamma}(t,x_0-y)\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1+(\beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-1/\alpha(x_0)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y),
\end{align*} where in the last inequality we used the fact that $\beta_0\geqslant\tilde \beta_0(x_0)>1-\alpha(x_0)$.

Combining all estimates together, we obtain that
\begin{equation*}
\int_0^t \left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\nabla p^z(t-s,x_0-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\right|\,ds
\preceq  \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y).
\end{equation*}
According to the estimate above and the dominated convergence theorem,  we know that
$\nabla p(t,\cdot)(x_0)$ exists, and \eqref{t5-1-1} holds by changing $\theta$ and $\gamma$ properly.

$$
and $$

\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{1-(1/\alpha_1)-\gamma}(t,x-z).
$$
In the following, we choose $\theta,\gamma$ small enough such that
$$\widehat \beta_0:={\alpha_1}\big(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta\big)/{\alpha(x_0)}>-1+(1/\alpha_1)+\gamma.$$

for every fixed $t \in (0,1]$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, $p(t,\cdot,y)$ is differentiable at $x_0\in \mathds R^d$ and
\eqref{t5-1-2} holds.

For $x,y,z\in \mathds R^d$ and any $\varepsilon>0$ \begin{align*} |p^{y+\varepsilon z}(t,x-y-\varepsilon)- p^{y}(t,x-y)| &\leqslant |p^{y+\varepsilon z}(t,x-y-\varepsilon)- p^{y+\varepsilon z}(t,x-y)|+ |p^{y+\varepsilon z}(t,x-y)-p^{y}(t,x-y)|. \end{align*} According to \eqref{p1-1-3} and \eqref{l4-1-1}, we can show that $(x,y)\mapsto p^y(t,x-y)$ is continuous. nodes.statement: Let $\beta_0^*\in(0,\beta_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}).$ Then, for any $0<\theta<\beta_0^*\alpha_1/\alpha_2$ and $0<\gamma<(\theta/\alpha_2)\wedge ((\beta_0^*/\alpha_2-\theta/\alpha_1)/2)$, $t\in (0,1]$ and $x\in\mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \bigg|\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\bigg|\preceq t+t^{(\beta_0^*/{\alpha_2})-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}. \end{equation} In particular, \begin{equation} \lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}\bigg|\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\bigg|=0. \end{equation}

nodes.statement: Throughout the proof, we will assume that $\beta_0<\alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$ for simplicity. Noting that $\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(t,x-y)\,dy=1$ for all $x\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$, we have \begin{align*} \bigg|\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\bigg|&=\bigg| \int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(t,x-y)\,dy\bigg|\\ &\leqslant \int_{\mathds R^d}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\ &\leqslant \int_{\{|x-y|\leqslant R_1\}}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\ &\quad +\int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\ &=:J_1+J_2, \end{align*} where $R_1$ is the constant in Lemma \ref{l4-1}. On the one hand, \eqref{l4-1-1} yields that \begin{align*} J_1& \preceq \int_{\mathds R^d} \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{1-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y)\,dy\preceq t^{(\beta_0/{\alpha_2})-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}, \end{align*} where the last inequality follows from the fact that \eqref{l3-1-1-00} holds for $\tilde \rho$. On the other hand, \begin{align*} J_2& \preceq \int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}\big(\rho^{x,0}_1(t,x-y)+\rho^{y,0}_1(t,x-y)\big)\,dy\\ &\preceq \int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}\bigg(\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(x)}}+\frac{t}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha(y)}}\bigg)\,dy\preceq t \int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}\frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dy \preceq t. \end{align*} Combining with both estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we prove \eqref{p4-1-1-e}. Choosing $\gamma,\theta>0$ small enough such that $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_1})<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, we immediately get \eqref{p4-1-1}.

nodes.statement:
Noting that $\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(t,x-y)\,dy=1$ for all $x\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$, we have
\begin{align*}
\bigg|\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-1\bigg|&=\bigg|
\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y(t,x-y)\,dy-\int_{\mathds R^d}p^x(t,x-y)\,dy\bigg|\\
&\leqslant \int_{\mathds R^d}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&\leqslant \int_{\{|x-y|\leqslant R_1\}}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&\quad +\int_{\{|x-y|>R_1\}}|p^x(t,x-y)-p^y(t,x-y)|\,dy\\
&=:J_1+J_2,
\end{align*}
where $R_1$ is the constant in Lemma \ref{l4-1}.

nodes.statement: For every $0<\varepsilon, \theta<\alpha_1$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\alpha_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\alpha_1}))/2)$, there are constants $R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,\theta)\in (0,1)$ and $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,\theta,\varepsilon)>0$ such that for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\big|\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz \leqslant c_1\tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y), \end{split} \end{equation} where $\tilde \rho$ is defined by \eqref{p3-1-7}.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\big|\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz \leqslant c_1\tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y), \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (5.3)
nodes.label: l4-2-1

nodes.statement: By using \eqref{l4-1-2}, we can verify that \begin{align*} & \delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\\ &=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^x(s,w) \big(\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\ &\quad+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\!\!\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w) \big(\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds. \end{align*} Therefore, \begin{align*} & \int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\big|\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ & \leqslant \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^x(s,w)\big| \bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\ &+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big| \bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\ &=:J_1+J_2. \end{align*} According to \eqref{p1-1-4} and \eqref{l4-1-5}, for every $\theta \in (0,1)$ and $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant $R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that for every $0<s<t<1$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\\ &\preceq \big[\left((t-s)^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|w|\right)^{\theta}\wedge 1\big]\cdot \left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right] \\ &\quad\times\big[ \rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w) +\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big]\\ &\preceq \left(|w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\right)\cdot \left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right] \cdot\big[ \rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w)\\ &\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad +\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big]. \end{split} \end{equation} Furthermore, following the argument of Lemma \ref{l1-1}, we can derive that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right] \cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y \pm z)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz \preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y),\\ &\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right] \cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz \preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y). \end{split} \end{equation} Combining \eqref{l4-1-4} with \eqref{l4-2-2} and \eqref{l4-2-3}, we find that for all $t\in(0,1]$ and $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$, \begin{align*} J_1 &\preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot \bigg[ \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\cdot \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y-w)\,dw\,ds\\ &\qquad\qquad\qquad+\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\cdot \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y)\,dw\,ds\bigg]\\ &=:|x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot(J_{11}+J_{12}). \end{align*} Since \eqref{l3-2-1-} holds true for $\tilde \rho$ as mentioned in Remark \ref{r3-3}(2), for every $0<\theta<\alpha_1$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\alpha_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\alpha_1}))/2)$, we have \begin{equation} \begin{split} J_{11}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,x-y) \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\big(s^{-1-\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_2})}(t-s)^{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})} +s^{-\gamma}(t-s)^{-1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\big)\,ds\\ &\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,x-y) \bigg(t^{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\int_0^{{t}/{2}}s^{-1-\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_2})}\,ds+ t^{-1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\int_0^{{t}/{2}} s^{-\gamma}\,ds\bigg)\\ & \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y). \end{split} \end{equation} On the other hand, note that for every $0<s<{t}/{2}$, $$\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y)\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).$$ Then, it holds that \begin{align*} J_{12}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y)\cdot \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\,dw\,ds\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y), \end{align*} where \eqref{l3-1-1-00} was used in the last inequality. Hence, we find that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$, \begin{equation*} J_1 \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y). \end{equation*} By estimates for the terms $$\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|$$ and $$\big| \delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|,$$ we can deal with the singularity as $s$ near $t$ by the same arguments above and obtain that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$, \begin{equation*} J_2 \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y). \end{equation*} Combining both of the estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we finally obtain that \eqref{l4-2-1} holds true.
nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2 (difference of second differences of p^x and p^y)
nodes.statement_short: Duhamel representation of δ_{p^x}-δ_{p^y}, split at t/2, and convolution estimates for ρ̃.

nodes.statement:
By using \eqref{l4-1-2}, we can verify that
\begin{align*}
& \delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\\
&=\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^x(s,w)
\big(\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds\\
&\quad+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\!\!\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)
\big(\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds.
\end{align*}
nodes.name: Duhamel representation
nodes.statement_short: Represent δ_{p^x}-δ_{p^y} as a time integral split at t/2.

nodes.statement:
Therefore,
\begin{align*}
& \int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\big|\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
& \leqslant \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^x(s,w)\big|
\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\
&+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|
\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{align*}
nodes.name: Split into J_1, J_2
nodes.statement_short: Integrate against |z|^{-d-α(x)}.

nodes.statement:
According to \eqref{p1-1-4} and \eqref{l4-1-5}, for every $\theta \in (0,1)$ and $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant
$R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that for every $0<s<t<1$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation} \begin{split}
&\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\\
&\preceq \big[\left((t-s)^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|w|\right)^{\theta}\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\\
&\quad\times\big[
\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w)
+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big]\\
&\preceq \left(|w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\right)\cdot
\left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
 \cdot\big[
\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w)\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad
+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}
nodes.name: Hölder bound of δ_{p^y}
nodes.statement_short: Bound increments of second differences in terms of ρ^{x,0}.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\\ &\preceq \big[\left((t-s)^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|w|\right)^{\theta}\wedge 1\big]\cdot \left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right] \\ &\quad\times\big[ \rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w) +\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big]\\ &\preceq \left(|w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\right)\cdot \left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right] \cdot\big[ \rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w)\\ &\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad +\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big]. \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (5.4)
nodes.label: l4-2-2

nodes.name: Integral bound
nodes.statement_short: Follow Lemma 2.3 for the z-integrals.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right] \cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y \pm z)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz \preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y),\\ &\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right] \cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz \preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y). \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (5.5)
nodes.label: l4-2-3

nodes.statement:
Combining \eqref{l4-1-4} with \eqref{l4-2-2} and \eqref{l4-2-3}, we find that for  all $t\in(0,1]$ and  $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{align*}
J_1 &\preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot \bigg[
\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\cdot
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad+\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\cdot
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y)\,dw\,ds\bigg]\\
&=:|x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot(J_{11}+J_{12}).
\end{align*}
nodes.name: Reduce J_1
Bound J_11
nodes.statement_short: Convolution inequality for ρ̃.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} J_{11}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,x-y) \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\big(s^{-1-\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_2})}(t-s)^{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})} +s^{-\gamma}(t-s)^{-1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\big)\,ds\\ &\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,x-y) \bigg(t^{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\int_0^{{t}/{2}}s^{-1-\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_2})}\,ds+ t^{-1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\int_0^{{t}/{2}} s^{-\gamma}\,ds\bigg)\\ & \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y). \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (5.6)
nodes.label: l4-2-3a

nodes.statement:
On the other hand, note that for every $0<s<{t}/{2}$, $$\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y)\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).$$
Then, it holds that
\begin{align*}
J_{12}&\preceq  \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y)\cdot
\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\,dw\,ds\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y),
\end{align*} where \eqref{l3-1-1-00} was used in the last inequality.
nodes.name: Bound J_12
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity in time and integrability of ρ̃.

nodes.name: Bound J_1
nodes.statement_short: Combine.

nodes.statement:
By estimates for
 the terms
$$\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|$$ and $$\big|
\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|,$$ we can deal with the singularity
as $s$ near $t$ by the same arguments above and obtain that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
J_2 \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).
\end{equation*}
nodes.name: Bound J_2
nodes.statement_short: Same argument near s=t.

nodes.statement: Combining both of the estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we finally obtain that \eqref{l4-2-1} holds true.
nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Gives (5.5).

nodes.statement: Let $\beta_0^*\in(0,\beta_0]\cap(0,{\alpha_2}).$ Then, we have the following two statements. \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then for every positive constants $\gamma,\theta \in (0,1)$ such that $\gamma<{\theta}/{\alpha_2}$ and $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_1})<\beta_0^*/\alpha_2$, there exists a constant $c_1:=c_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma,\theta)>0$ such that for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \Big|\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,x-y)\,dy\Big|\leqslant c_1t^{-1+(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}. \end{equation} \item[(2)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$, then for every positive constants $\gamma,\theta \in (0,1)$ such that $\gamma<{\theta}/{\alpha_2}$ and $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_1})<\beta_0^*/\alpha_2$, the estimate \eqref{p4-2-1} will be replaced by \begin{equation} \Big|\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,x-y)\,dy\Big|\leqslant c_1\big( t^{-1+(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}+t^{1-{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}}\big). \end{equation} \end{itemize}
nodes.name: Lemma 5.3 (integral of L^x p^y)
nodes.statement_short: |∫ L^x p^y(t,x-y) dy| ≤ c t^{-1+(β_0^*/α_2)-2γ-θ/α_1} (plus t^{1-α_2/α_1} for general κ).
nodes.label: p4-2

nodes.statement: \Big|\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,x-y)\,dy\Big|\leqslant c_1t^{-1+(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}.
nodes.name: Equation (5.7)
nodes.label: p4-2-1

nodes.statement: \Big|\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,x-y)\,dy\Big|\leqslant c_1\big( t^{-1+(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}+t^{1-{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}}\big).
nodes.name: Equation (5.8)
nodes.label: p4-2-1a

nodes.statement: We assume that $\beta_0<\alpha_2$ and $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$ for simplicity. Observe that \begin{align*} \int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,x-y)\,dy &=\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,x-y)- {\mathcal L}^xp^x(t,x-y)\big)\,dy\\ &=\int_{\mathds R^d} \int_{\mathds R^d}\big(\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z) -\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)\big)\cdot\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\,dy. \end{align*} Therefore, for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{align*} \Big|\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^xp^y(t,x-y)\,dy\Big| &\preceq \int_{\{|y-x|\leqslant R_1\}}\int_{\mathds R^d} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z) -\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\,dy\\ &\quad+\int_{\{|y-x|>R_1\}}\int_{\mathds R^d}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z) -\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\,dy\\ &=:J_1+J_2, \end{align*} where $R_1$ is the constant in Lemma \ref{l4-2}. According to \eqref{l4-2-1}, we have for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{align*} J_1& \preceq \int_{\{|y-x|\leqslant R_1\}}\tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y)\,dy \preceq t^{-1+(\beta_0^*/\alpha_2)-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}, \end{align*} where we used the fact that \eqref{l3-1-1-00} holds for $\tilde \rho$. (1) Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. Then, according to the argument for $J_1$ in \eqref{l2-1-3a}, for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|>R_1$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_{\mathds R^d}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\\ & \int_{\mathds R^d}|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\end{split} \end{equation} which imply that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{align*} J_2&\preceq \int_{\{|y-x|>R_2\}}\int_{\mathds R^d} |\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\,dy +\int_{\{|y-x|>R_2\}}\int_{\mathds R^d} |\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\,dy\\ &\leqslant C_1. \end{align*} Combining both the estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we prove \eqref{p4-2-1}. (2) When $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$, by the argument of \eqref{l2-1-5}, the first inequality in \eqref{p4-2-2} will be changed into \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathds R^d}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\preceq \frac{t^{1-{(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}}}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}}. \end{equation*} Using this inequality and following the same line as above, we will obtain \eqref{p4-2-1a}.
nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3 (integral of L^x p^y)
nodes.statement_short: Write the integral as ∫(δ_{p^y}-δ_{p^x}) and split |x-y| ≤ R_1 (Lemma 5.2) and > R_1 (far-field bounds).

nodes.name: Reduce and split
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the integral via δ_{p^y}-δ_{p^x} and bound the near part by Lemma 5.2.

nodes.name: (1) κ independent of z
nodes.statement_short: Far part bounded by a constant.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\int_{\mathds R^d}|\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\\ & \int_{\mathds R^d}|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\preceq \frac{1}{|x-y|^{d+\alpha_1}},\end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (5.9)
nodes.label: p4-2-2

nodes.name: (2) General κ
nodes.statement_short: Far part acquires the factor t^{1-α_2/α_1}.

nodes.statement: The following two statements hold. \begin{itemize} \item [(1)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$, then $p(t,x,y)$ defined by \eqref{eq2-1} satisfies the equation \eqref{t1-1-1} pointwise. \item[(2)] If $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$ and ${(\alpha_2/\alpha_1)}-1<\min\{{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2},{1}/{2}\}$, then $p(t,x,y)$ also satisfies the equation \eqref{t1-1-1} pointwise. \end{itemize}
nodes.name: Proposition 5.4 (p solves the heat equation)
nodes.statement_short: The Levi-constructed p satisfies ∂_t p = L p(t,·,y)(x) pointwise.
conclusions: $p(t,x,y)$ defined by \eqref{eq2-1} satisfies the equation \eqref{t1-1-1} pointwise
nodes.label: t4-1

nodes.statement: For simplicity, we assume that $\beta_0< {\alpha_2}/{2}$ and $\beta_0^*=\beta_0$. {(1)} We first assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$. The proof is split into four parts. {(i)} For every $0<s<t<1$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$, define \begin{equation*} \phi(t,s,x,y):=\int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz, \end{equation*} where $q(t,x,y)$ is constructed in Proposition \ref{p3-1}. By \eqref{eq2-1}, it holds that \begin{equation} p(t,x,y)=p^y(t,x-y)+\int_0^t \phi(t,s,x,y)\,ds. \end{equation} Note that for every $t \in (0,1]$, $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ and $\varepsilon>0$, \begin{align*} \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\phi(t+\varepsilon,s,x,y)\,ds-q(t,x,y) &= \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t+\varepsilon-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds-q(t,x,y)\\ &=\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t+\varepsilon-s,x-z)\big( q(s,z,y)-q(s,x,y)\big)\,dz\,ds\\ &\quad +\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\bigg( \int_{\mathds R^d} p^z(t+\varepsilon-s,x-z)\,dz\bigg)\cdot \big(q(s,x,y)-q(t,x,y)\big)\,ds\\ &\quad +q(t,x,y)\cdot\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d} p^z(t+\varepsilon-s,x-z)\,dz-1\bigg)\,ds\\ &=:J_1(\varepsilon)+J_2(\varepsilon)+J_3(\varepsilon). \end{align*} First, by \eqref{p3-1-1a}, for every $t>0$, $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ and $\sigma>0$, there exists a constant $\varepsilon_1:=\varepsilon_1(t,x,y, \sigma)>0$ such that for all $z\in \mathds R^d$ with $|z-x|\leqslant \varepsilon_1$, \begin{equation} |q(s,z,y)-q(s,x,y)|\leqslant \sigma \end{equation} holds for all $t<s<t+\varepsilon$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$. Let \begin{align*} |J_1(\varepsilon)|&\preceq \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\int_{\{|z-x|\leqslant \varepsilon_1\}}p^z(t+\varepsilon-s,x-z)\big| q(s,z,y)-q(s,x,y)\big|\,dz\,ds\\ &\quad +\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\int_{\{|z-x|>\varepsilon_1\}}p^z(t+\varepsilon-s,x-z)\big| q(s,z,y)-q(s,x,y)\big|\,dz\,ds\\ &=:J_{11}(\varepsilon)+J_{12}(\varepsilon). \end{align*} According to \eqref{t4-1-2} and \eqref{l3-1-1}, we know immediately that \begin{align*} J_{11}(\varepsilon)&\preceq \sigma\cdot\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_{1} (t+\varepsilon-s,x-z)\,dz\,ds\preceq \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon}\cdot \int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\,ds \leqslant C_1 \sigma, \end{align*} where $C_1>0$ is a constant independent of $\varepsilon$ and $\sigma$. At the same time, it holds that for any $\gamma<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2},$ \begin{align*} |J_{12}(\varepsilon)|&\preceq \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\cdot\bigg( \int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\big(t+\varepsilon-s\big) \int_{\{|z-x|>\varepsilon_1\}} \frac{|q(s,z,y)|+|q(s,x,y)|}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dz\,ds\bigg)\\ &\preceq \varepsilon_1^{-d-\alpha_1}\int_t^{t+\varepsilon} \int_{\mathds R^d}\big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\big)(s,z-y)\,dz\,ds\\ &\quad +\int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\int_{\{|z-x|>\varepsilon_1\}} \frac{\big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\big)(s,x-y)}{|z-x|^{d+\alpha_1}}\,dz\,ds\\ &\preceq \varepsilon_1^{-d-\alpha_1}\bigg( \int_t^{t+\varepsilon}s^{-1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\,ds+\varepsilon_1^d t^{-1-({d}/{\alpha_1})-\gamma} \int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\,ds\bigg)\\ &\leqslant C(\varepsilon_1)t^{-1-({d}/{\alpha_1})-\gamma}\varepsilon, \end{align*} where in the first inequality we used the fact that $p^z(t,x)\preceq \frac{t}{|x|^{d+\alpha_1}}$ for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x|>\varepsilon_1$, the second inequality follows from \eqref{p3-1-1}, and in the third inequality we used \eqref{l3-1-1-00} and the fact that $\rho^{y,0}_{-\gamma}(s,x)\preceq t^{-1-({d}/{\alpha_1})-\gamma}$ for all $t<s<t+\varepsilon$ and $x\in \mathds R^d$. Second, note that for every fixed $x,y \in \mathds R^d$, $q_0(\cdot,x,y)$ is continuous in $(0,1]$. Then, by \eqref{eq2-2}, \eqref{p3-1-1} and the dominated convergence theorem, we know that $q(\cdot,x,y)$ is continuous in $(0,1]$. Thus, for every $t \in (0,1]$, $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ and $\sigma>0$, there exists a constant $\varepsilon_2:=\varepsilon_2(t,x,y,\sigma)>0$ such that for all $|s-t|<\varepsilon_2$, \begin{equation*} |q(s,x,y)-q(t,x,y)|\leqslant \sigma, \end{equation*} from which we have that when $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_2$, \begin{align*} |J_2(\varepsilon)|&\preceq \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon}\cdot \Big(\int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\Big|\int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t+\varepsilon-s,x-z)\,dz\Big|\,ds\Big)\leqslant C_2\sigma, \end{align*} where in the last inequality we have used Lemma \ref{p4-1}, and $C_2>0$ is a constant independent of $\varepsilon$ and $\sigma$. Third, according to Lemma \ref{p4-1}, we arrive at \begin{align*} \lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}|J_3(\varepsilon)|&\leqslant |q(t,x,y)|\cdot \bigg(\lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \cdot \int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\Big|\int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(t+\varepsilon-s,x-z)\,dz-1\Big|\,ds\bigg)\\ &\leqslant |q(t,x,y)|\cdot\bigg(\lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}\sup_{s \in (0,\varepsilon)} \Big|\int_{\mathds R^d}p^z(s,x-z)\,dz-1\Big|\bigg)=0. \end{align*} Combining all the estimates together, we arrive at for every $\sigma>0$, \begin{align*} \lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}\Big|\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\phi(t+\varepsilon,s,x,y)\,ds-q(t,x,y)\Big|\leqslant C_3\sigma, \end{align*} where $C_3$ is independent of $\varepsilon$ and $\sigma$. Since $\sigma$ is arbitrary, we finally obtain that \begin{equation} \begin{split} \lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}\Big|\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\int_t^{t+\varepsilon}\phi(t+\varepsilon,s,x,y)\,ds-q(t,x,y)\Big|=0. \end{split} \end{equation} {(ii)} By the proof of \eqref{l4-2-3} (also see \cite[Theorem 2.4]{CZ}), it holds that \begin{equation} | {\mathcal L}^zp^z(t-s,x-z)|\preceq \rho^{z,0}_0(t-s,x-z), \end{equation} and so we can verify that for every $0<s<t<1$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, $$\int_{\mathds R^d}| {\mathcal L}^z p^z(t-s,x-z)||q(s,z,y)|\,dz<\infty.$$ Thus, by the dominated convergence theorem, for every $0<s<t$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \partial_t \phi(t,s,x,y)&=\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^zp^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\\ &=\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^zp^z(t-s,x-z)(q(s,z,y)-q(s,x,y))\,dz\\ &\quad +q(s,x,y)\int_{\mathds R^d}( {\mathcal L}^z- {\mathcal L}^x)p^z(t-s,x-z)\,dz\\ &\quad +q(s,x,y)\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^x p^z(t-s,x-z)\,dz\\ &=:\tilde J_1+ \tilde J_2+ \tilde J_3. \end{split} \end{equation} Combining \eqref{t4-1-4} with \eqref{p3-1-1a} yields that for any $0<\gamma<\theta<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$, \begin{align*} |\tilde J_1| &\preceq \int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{z,\tilde \theta}_0(t-s,x-z)\cdot \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})}(s,z-y)\,dz\\ &\quad +\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{z,\tilde \theta}_0(t-s,x-z)\cdot \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})}(s,x-y)\,dz\\ &=:\tilde J_{11}+ \tilde J_{12}, \end{align*} where $\tilde \theta:=\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)/{\alpha_2}$. According to \eqref{l3-2-1} (which holds for $\tilde \rho$), we obtain that for every ${t}/{2}\leqslant s \leqslant t$, \begin{align*} \tilde J_{11}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\cdot\big[(t-s)^{-1+({\tilde \theta}/{\alpha_2})}s^{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})-1}\big]\preceq t^{-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})-({d}/{\alpha_1})-2}(t-s)^{-1+({\tilde \theta}/{\alpha_2})}, \end{align*} where in the last inequality we have used the fact that $\tilde\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\preceq t^{-1-d/\alpha_1}$ and $s^{-1}\preceq t^{-1}$ for ${t}/{2}\leqslant s \leqslant t$. Note that $\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})}(s,x-y)\preceq t^{-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}$ for every ${t}/{2}\leqslant s \leqslant t$, and \eqref{l3-1-1} holds for $\tilde \rho$, then we have \begin{align*} \tilde J_{12}& \preceq t^{-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{z,\tilde \theta}_{0}(t-s,x-z)\,dz\preceq t^{-\gamma-({\beta_0}/{\alpha_1})-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}(t-s)^{-1+({\tilde \theta}/{\alpha_2})}. \end{align*} By \eqref{l2-1-2} and \eqref{p3-1-1}, we arrive at that for any $0<\gamma<\theta<{\beta_0}/{\alpha_2}$ and every ${t}/{2}\leqslant s \leqslant t$, \begin{equation*} |( {\mathcal L}^z- {\mathcal L}^x)p^z(t-s,x-z)|\preceq |q_0(t-s,x, z)|\preceq \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(t-s,x-z) \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} |q(s,x,y)|\preceq \big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\big)(s,x-y)\preceq t^{-\gamma-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}. \end{equation*} Hence, combining both estimates above with \eqref{l3-1-1}, we obtain \begin{align*} |\tilde J_{2}|&\preceq t^{-\gamma-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}\int_{\mathds R^d} \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(t-s,x-z)\,dz \preceq t^{-\gamma-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}(t-s)^{-1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}. \end{align*} Furthermore, \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{p4-2-1} yield that for every ${t}/{2}\leqslant s \leqslant t$ and constants $\gamma,\theta \in (0,1)$ such that $\gamma<{\theta}/{\alpha_2}$ and $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_1})<\beta_0/\alpha_2$, \begin{equation*} |\tilde J_3| \preceq t^{-\gamma-({d}/{\alpha_1})-1}(t-s)^{-1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}. \end{equation*} On the other hand, when $0<s\leqslant {t}/{2}$, it follows from \eqref{t4-1-4}, \eqref{p3-1-1} and \eqref{l3-2-1} that \begin{align*} \big|\partial_t \phi(t,s,x,y)\big| &\preceq \int_{\mathds R^d}\big| {\mathcal L}^z p^z(t-s,x-z)\big|\big|q(s,z,y)\big|\,dz\\ &\preceq \int_{\mathds R^d} \rho^{z,0}_0(t-s,x-z)\cdot \big(\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}\big)(s,z-y)\,dz\\ &\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\cdot\big[(t-s)^{-1}s^{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}+ (t-s)^{-1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})}s^{-\gamma}+s^{-1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}\big]\\ &\quad +\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{0}(t,x-y)\cdot(t-s)^{-1}s^{-\gamma}\\ &\preceq t^{-2-({d}/{\alpha_1})}s^{-1+({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}, \end{align*} where in the last inequality we have used the facts that $\rho^{y,0}_0(t,x-y)\preceq t^{-1-({d}/{\alpha_1})}$ and $(t-s)^{-1}\preceq t^{-1}$ for every $0<s\leqslant {t}/{2}$. Therefore, choosing $\gamma,\theta \in (0,1)$ such that $\gamma<{\theta}/{\alpha_2}$ and $2\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_1})<\beta_0/\alpha_2$, and combining all the estimates above, we know that \eqref{e:lkk} is well defined, and that for every $t \in (0,1)$, $ \sup_{t_0 \in (t,t+\varepsilon_1)}| \partial_t\phi(t_0,s,x,y)|\leqslant \eta(t,s), $ where $\eta$ is a non-negative measurable function such that $\int_0^t \eta(t,s)\,ds<\infty$ and $\varepsilon_1>0$ is a constant small enough (which may depend on $t$). Now, according to the dominated convergence theorem, for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\cdot \bigg(\int_0^t \big(\phi(t+\varepsilon,s,x,y)-\phi(t,s,x,y)\big)\,ds\bigg)= \int_0^t \partial_t \phi(t,s,x,y)\,ds. \end{split} \end{equation} {(iii)} We obtain by \eqref{t4-1-3} and \eqref{t4-1-5} that for every $t \in (0,1)$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{align*} &\lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}\Bigg|\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \cdot \Big(\int_0^{t+\varepsilon}\phi(t+\varepsilon,s,x,y)\,ds- \int_0^{t}\phi(t,s,x,y)\,ds\Big)-q(t,x,y)-\int_0^t \partial_t \phi(t,s,x,y)\,ds\Bigg|\\ &\leqslant \lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}\Bigg|\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\cdot\Big(\int_t^{t+\varepsilon} \phi(t+\varepsilon,s,x,y)\,ds\Big)-q(t,x,y)\Bigg|\\ &\quad+\lim_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}\Bigg|\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\cdot\Big(\int_0^{t} (\phi(t+\varepsilon,s,x,y)-\phi(t,s,x,y))\,ds\Big)-\int_0^t \partial_t \phi(t,s,x,y)\,ds\Bigg|\\ &=0. \end{align*} By the same way, it is not difficult to verify \begin{align*} &\lim_{\varepsilon \uparrow 0}\Bigg|\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \cdot \Big(\int_0^{t+\varepsilon}\phi(t+\varepsilon,s,x,y)\,ds- \int_0^{t}\phi(t,s,x,y)\,ds\Big)-q(t,x,y)-\int_0^t \partial_t \phi(t,s,x,y)\,ds\Bigg|=0. \end{align*} Hence, we have for any $t_0\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation*} \partial_t\left(\int_0^{\cdot}\phi(\cdot,s,x,y)\,ds\right)(t_0)=q(t_0,x,y)+\int_0^{t_0}\partial_t \phi(t_0,s,x,y)\,ds. \end{equation*} Combining all estimates above with \eqref{t4-1-1}, \eqref{eq2-2} and \eqref{e:lkk}, we have for every $t \in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \frac{\partial p(t,x,y)}{\partial t} &= {\mathcal L}^y p^y(t,x-y)+q(t,x,y)+\int_0^t \partial_t \phi(t,s,x,y)\,ds\\ &= {\mathcal L}^y p^y(t,x-y)+( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y)p^y(t,x-y)\\ &\quad +\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d}( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^z)p^z(t-s,x-z)\cdot q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\\ &\quad +\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^z p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds\\ &= {\mathcal L}^x p^y(t,x-y)+\int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^x p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds. \end{split} \end{equation} Furthermore, by the same arguments for estimates of $\tilde J_1$, $\tilde J_2$ and $\tilde J_3$ above, we have \begin{equation} \begin{split} & \int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}| {\mathcal L}^x p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\ &\preceq \int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\big| {\mathcal L}^z p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\big|\,dz\,ds+\int_0^t \int_{\mathds R^d}|( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^z) p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)|\,dz\,ds\\ &<\infty \end{split} \end{equation} and so $$\int_0^t {\mathcal L}^x(\phi(t,s,\cdot,y))(x)\,ds= \int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^x p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds,$$ which in turn implies that \eqref{t4-1-6} is well defined. {(iv)} For any $\varepsilon,\sigma>0$ small enough, \begin{align*} &\int_{\{|z|>\sigma\}}\delta_{\int_0^t\phi(t,s,\cdot,y)\,ds}(x;z)\cdot\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\ &=\int_{\varepsilon}^{t-\varepsilon} \int_{\{|z|>\sigma\}}\delta_{\phi(t,s,\cdot,y)}(x;z)\cdot\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz \,ds +\int_{\{(0,\varepsilon)\cup(t-\varepsilon,t)\}} \int_{\{|z|>\sigma\}}\delta_{\phi(t,s,\cdot,y)}(x;z)\cdot\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz \,ds\\ &=:\widehat J_1(\varepsilon,\sigma)+\widehat J_2(\varepsilon,\sigma). \end{align*} Note that for the integral with respect to time variable in $\widehat J_1(\varepsilon,\sigma)$, there is not any singularity. According to the dominated convergence theorem, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{\sigma \downarrow 0}J_1(\varepsilon,\sigma)&=\int_{\varepsilon}^{t-\varepsilon} {\mathcal L}^x(\phi(t,s,\cdot,y))(x)\,ds=\int_{\varepsilon}^{t-\varepsilon}\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^x p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds, \end{align*} Meanwhile, according to the proof of \eqref{t4-1-7a} and Fatou's lemma we arrive at \begin{equation*} \limsup_{\sigma \downarrow 0}|\widehat J_2(\varepsilon,\sigma)|\leqslant \int_{\{(0,\varepsilon)\cup(t-\varepsilon,t)\}}| {\mathcal L}^x(\phi(t,s,\cdot,y)(x)|\,ds. \end{equation*} Hence, combining all the estimates above with \eqref{e2-3} yields \begin{align*} &\Big| {\mathcal L}^x\Big(\int_0^t \phi(t,s,\cdot,y)\,ds\Big)(x)- \int_0^t {\mathcal L}^x(\phi(t,s,\cdot,y))(x)\,ds\Big|\\ &\leqslant \limsup_{\sigma \downarrow 0}\bigg|\int_{\{|z|>\sigma\}}\delta_{\int_0^t\phi(t,s,\cdot,y)\,ds}(x;z)\cdot\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz -\int_0^t {\mathcal L}^x(\phi(t,s,\cdot,y))(x)\,ds \bigg|\\ &\leqslant 2\int_{\{(0,\varepsilon)\cup(t-\varepsilon,t)\}}| {\mathcal L}^x(\phi(t,s,\cdot,y))(x)|\,ds. \end{align*} Then, letting $\varepsilon \rightarrow 0$, we know that for every $t \in (0,1)$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$, \begin{align*} {\mathcal L}^x\Big(\int_0^t \phi(t,s,\cdot,y)\,ds\Big)(x) &=\int_0^t {\mathcal L}^x(\phi(t,s,\cdot,y))(x)\,ds= \int_0^t\int_{\mathds R^d} {\mathcal L}^x p^z(t-s,x-z)q(s,z,y)\,dz\,ds, \end{align*} which along with \eqref{t4-1-6} yields \eqref{t1-1-1} immediately. {(2)} Suppose that $\kappa(x,z)$ depends on $z$. Then, using \eqref{l2-1-1}, \eqref{p3-1-2} and \eqref{p3-1-2a}, and following the same arguments above, we can also show \eqref{t1-1-1} holds true. The details are omitted here.
